ST2 (from the D01-B2 lift, not before D01-B2): PROP-01 is gone, and its empty spot shows the dry tray. Nothing else moves.
Locked in D01-B2 only. If a later frame finds it, it is in ST2.

props.description:
Paper cone filters in bleached white crepe #F1EEE6, loose, with no box and no print, so packaging never enters a frame. They live in the upper cabinet (y 116-200) and never sit on the counter. Opened, a filter is about Ø 9 cm at the mouth and about 10 cm long (ASSUMED, size 02).

- Collar on the gloss rim band #C9A77E: 1.9:1, plus crepe against gloss.
- Collar on the wall: 4.5:1.
- Bloom #2E1E14 in the white paper: 13.8:1.
Appears in no other location.
props.persistent_state_notes:

D02-2: none.

props.description:
Stovetop gooseneck kettle, 0.9 L: a squat cylinder, Ø 13 × 11 cm, with a domed lid, an oiled beech knob #9C7650, a riveted loop handle in oiled beech and a spout tip of Ø 5 mm.
Finish: terracotta matte enamel #A4583F everywhere, spout included, so there is no bare steel and no mirror path.
Wear: a 1 cm scorch band at the base, #6E3A2A, from the gas flame of RANGE-01's front burner every morning. It is the S2 detail, framed in D02-1 only.
No maker stamp. It reads 3.7:1 against the cream dripper.
Appears in no other location.
props.persistent_state_notes:
ST1 (D01-B1 to D01-B2): heating on RANGE-01's front burner at 212/97 in the story. The range is not built, so props fill it hot, off-set, for each take.

props.description:
Counter top: white-oak butcher block, 4 cm thick, 15 strips of 4.2 cm running along y (x 197.0-260). It is finished with a tobacco-brown tinted hardwax oil, matte, to #533C2B (in the story, the landlord's refinish before she moved in; ASSUMED). Top at 91 cm, front edge eased to 2 mm. The seams at x = 260 − 4.2n are flush 0.5 mm #3B2B1F glue hairlines.
Grommet: a Ø 2.0 cm hole through the back strip at 258/322 with a flush black ring #2A2C2E, for PROP-08.
The work zone (y 250-340) is clean oiled oak, with no rings, stains, drip spots or knife marks, so no frame shows a mark the product made.
- Mark 2 (texture only): front-edge wear at x 197-201, y 250-330, where her forearms rest while she brews. The tint is worn off the arris to satin #7E6045 (1.8:1), rounded to about a 6 mm radius.
- Mark 3: a blue-black iron-water stain #25201C (1.6:1), 3 × 8 cm, at the sink's front corner, 204/185, from a wet cast-iron pan.
Appears in no other location.
props.persistent_state_notes:
ST1 (D01-B1 until the D01-B4a set-down; D02-1): 232.7/280 is clean bare oiled #533C2B oak. PROP-03 stands at 232.7/295.
ST2 (from the D01-B4a set-down, not before D01-B4a; D01-B5 to D01-B6; D02-2): PROP-01's foot stands on 232.7/280. From D01-B5, the mug's footprint at 232.7/295 is clean bare oak. The clear zone has no crumbs, dust, grounds or fingerprints, and the seams are closed hairlines.

props.description:
Charging cable and adapter: a 1 m USB-C cable with a straight plug and a black matte TPE jacket #2A2C2E, unbranded, plus a blank black cube adapter in OUT-01 under the top. It shows why the phone is waiting on this counter at 7:00: it charged here overnight, not by her bed. It reads 1.4:1 on the oak, below the product body's 7.3:1.
Appears in no other location.
props.persistent_state_notes:
ST1 (D01-B1, until the flip at about 0.8 s): the plug is in the ST1 port at 222.3/304.8. The cable runs out along the phone's axis to x 218, then along x 218 toward wall C through a loose loop (x 210-218, y 308-318, about 10 cm of slack) to y 322. From there it runs along y 322 to x 258 and down through the grommet at 258/322 to the adapter in OUT-01, below the top. D02-2: struck.

locations.product_placement:
Where it works: in the PROP-07 work zone at the wall-C end of the counter, never on a plinth.
- It enters standing in the rack at 232.7/213 and is first seen in D01-B2's first angle; the D01-B1 hand exits toward it.
- It brews on PROP-03 at 232.7/295, 45 cm from wall C (D01-B2 seat to D01-B4a; D02-1).
- It rests at 232.7/280, 60 cm from wall C, on the far side of the mug from the phone, so the phone, the mug and the dripper sit in a line (D01-B4a to D01-B6; D02-2).
D01-B2 carries it 82 cm and D01-B4a carries it 15 cm, both along the x 232.7 strip centre and never turned in the hand. The front (the thickest 4 cm arc of the glaze pool, the mark her thumb crosses in D01-B2) faces 235°, toward the aisle and wall A, in every state.
Its job changes PROP-04 ST1→ST2 and PROP-03 ST1→ST2 in D01-B2. It takes the filter in the D01-B2/D01-B3 cut (PROP-05 ST2), and its D01-B4a set-down changes PROP-07 ST1→ST2.

Swap test: the uneven glaze pool at the foot (gloss #B59A72, 3-12 mm). It is under her thumb in D01-B2 and faces the lens at 235° in D01-B5, D01-B6 and D02-2. It exists because the piece is hand-glazed (verified); an evenly machine-glazed same-tier cone has a level glaze line. It is the only swap test.

Contrast under an even key (18% grey card #767676):
- Body #E3D9C6 on the oak #533C2B: 7.3:1. On the backsplash #6B6E67: 3.7:1.
- At the base, on the oak: the pool is 3.8:1 and the raw flange edge #A88663 is 3.1:1. The pool on the flange is 1.25:1, carried by gloss over matte.
- On the white mug #F2EFE8 the body is only 1.2:1. The raw band hanging 2 mm outside the rim separates them at 2.9:1, and the pool at 2.3:1: a finish change from satin to gloss to raw.
- Pool against the body: 1.9:1, plus satin against gloss.
- Top edge in D01-B3 and D02-1: the collar #F1EEE6 on the rim band #C9A77E is 1.9:1, plus crepe against gloss. The collar on the wall is 4.5:1, and the bloom in the white filter is 13.8:1.
- Everything else in the hero frame reads lower than the body: the phone #77756F on the oak at 2.2:1, the cable #2A2C2E at 1.4:1 (off frame in D01-B5 to D01-B6), and TILE-01 on the paint at 3.6:1, never behind the dripper's outline.

Mirror path, in section and plan. Only the pool, the rim band and the mug glaze are gloss (about 5%). The pool fills the fillet between the cone wall (normal 18° below horizontal) and the flange top (normal straight up), so in section it faces every elevation from −18° to 90°. For a lens at elevation θ above the pool (92 cm) on the front's 235° bearing, a normal at elevation φ mirrors elevation 2φ − θ; values above 90° carry over the zenith onto the far side (bearing 55°).
- Below 0°: the oak top in front of the foot, out to the front edge (x 197, 44 cm).
- 0° to 32.8°: the wall-B flat at y ≈ 117, 92-275 cm (the flat runs full height, so there is no gap).
- At θ: the lens itself; a flag with a lens port is the DP's.
- 32.8° to 90°: CEIL-01, from wall B to overhead.
- 90° to 100°: CEIL-01 over the counter to wall D.
- 100° to 180° − θ: wall D from 275 cm down to 92 + 33.3·tan θ cm, which is 104 cm at θ 20°, 111 at 30° and 120 at 40°. From θ ≈ 30°, the pool's up-facing top catches TILE-01's 112 cm edge as a thin pale line on the gloss, which helps the swap test read.
In plan, the front's ±30° (normals 205-265°) fans the reflection over bearings 175-295°: down the counter to the wall-A flat (175-220°), the wall-B flat (220-285°) and the wall-C flat beside WIN-01 (285-295°). The flank toward wall D (normals 145-205°) sees the backsplash, TILE-01, the upper-cabinet end panel and the rack. The flank toward wall C (normals about 272-306°) sees the WIN-01 opening, which is the key's diffusion frame and so the DP's glint. At the pool's size (3-12 mm) only tone masses read, so bare flats stand in for the unbuilt range, fridge and door. The coffee mirrors wall D: bare paint and TILE-01's edge, with no outlet or cable. Any light in these paths is a DP request.

Clear zone for D01-B5 to D01-B6 and D02-2: x 221.7-243.7, y 269-291, 0-25 cm above the top. Nothing in it moves. The phone lies 8 cm beyond it and reads lower than the product, and the cable is off frame. No plaques, tags, price cards or packaging appear, and the exterior carries no logo. Supers are composited and never placed over the dripper. No paid image shows a mark the product made.

assumptions: ASSUMED: USA, 2026, a pre-war rental, from the USD price and 'link in bio'. That locks NEMA 5-15 at OUT-01 (in no frame), a gas range (the source of the kettle's scorch band), a 12-hour '7:00' and a USB-C phone. No window view, signage, street or plates appear.

LOC-01 is a studio BUILD that a small crew can put up next week (ASSUMED). It consists of the counter run with the sink cut-out, the wall-D backsplash with the upper cabinets and TILE-01, full-height bare flats on walls A, B and C (with the WIN-01 opening in C), and CEIL-01. The wall-A flat, the full-height wall-B flat and CEIL-01 were added this round because the glaze pool and the mug glaze mirror almost the whole room. At their size only tone masses read, so bare flats stand in for the appliances. RANGE-01, FRIDGE-01, FAUCET-01, DOOR-01 and the base cabinet at y 0-40 are placed in plan but not built.

Screen direction is solved in the plan. With the run on wall D, the rack lies at frame right of the mug as seen from the aisle, so the D01-B2 carry runs right to left. The flop-safe dressing stays as a fallback.

The script lands the phone against the mug and sets the dripper down on the far side of the mug (D01-B1, D01-B4a). That fixes the phone, the port and the cable route. The cable rule is 'never enters y < 302', and the cable drops through the grommet at 258/322 to OUT-01 below the top.

Mark 1, Mark 1b and the secondary swap test are cut. From D01-B1 to D01-B4a they showed a stain and a drip spot the product had made on oiled wood, which is an unverified negative claim built on an ASSUMED raw foot, and hiding them needed a ±3 mm set-down that no take holds. 232.7/280 is clean oak in every state, and the glaze pool, which rests on the verified 'hand-glazed', is the only swap test. The D01-B4a set-down now needs ±1 cm, and props reset the exact mark for D01-B5 across the script's 'moments later'. Props drain the cone before the D01-B4a take, so the script's last drip is the only one.

No filter is on the counter before D01-B3. The pre-opened filter is cut for two reasons. 'Started the ritual before the phone lit' contradicted the S1 turn ('her five minutes start here'). And its spot past the phone would have sent her hand over the phone, which the script rules out. The filter and grounds go in during the D01-B2/D01-B3 cut, as the script decides. The S1 detail is now PROP-03's tide line. The earlier question about a filter fetch inside D01-B2 is withdrawn.

The oak deepens from #7A5A3E to #533C2B. That is one step past the review's suggested #5A4230, so the raw flange also clears 3:1 (3.1:1, where #5A4230 gives 2.8:1). The body moves from 4.5:1 to 7.3:1 on the oak and the pool from 2.3:1 to 3.8:1; the body stays at 3.7:1 on the backsplash and the raw band at 2.9:1 on the mug. The phone bumper moves from charcoal #3E4447 (1.0:1 on the new oak) to stone grey #77756F (2.2:1), so the S4 phone still reads and still sits below the product. The black cable drops to 1.4:1, also below the product. The seams, Mark 2 and Mark 3 are re-coloured to read on the darker oak.

TILE-01 is a cool sage-grey #D5D8D2 rather than the review's #DCD6CA, because the bible reserves cream for the product. It keeps the same 3.6:1 on the paint. It stays empty, adds no lock, stops 5.5 cm below the reserved card area and never backs the dripper's outline for a lens at or above the rim (99.5 cm).

The coffee mirror line and the pool's section path are computed from the plan: coffee at 98.5 cm, pool at 92 cm, cone wall 18° off vertical (ASSUMED). They were not measured. Lens placement stays the DP's, and the prelight check is in blockers.

This department reserves the wall-D card area (paint from 125 cm up, y 240-340) for composited cards. Where the cards sit is the storyboard's call; if they need to sit lower, TILE-01 moves, not the card.

The WIN-01 translight stays struck. The pool's wall-C flank sees the WIN-01 opening, but the key's diffusion frame fills it, so nothing beyond it can show. Reinstate the translight and its rights item only if the prelight finds something beyond the diffusion in a reflection.
S4's real detail is the phone left face-down where she flipped it (script D01-B5: 'the phone lies face-down and dark'). Mark 2 is texture only. D02-2 stays bare on purpose as the DTC image.

PROP-04 is dressed dry as the dripper's everyday resting spot, with no sponge, soap, suds, standing water or cutlery cup. No story line says the dripper is hand-washed, so the set never contradicts D02-2's 'it still goes in the dishwasher' (verified: dishwasher safe).
The lock screen carries the script's one generic banner, too small to read, drawn as blank shapes with no glyphs.
D01-B4b timing follows the script: the buzz, glow and rings run about 8.5-9.5 s, and the card comes up at 9.5 s.

In D01-B4b the hand rests on finger pads only, on the glaze over 225-315° below the rim, palm clear, with the heel on the oak 3 cm in front of the mug. The script notes that a full wrap would damp the rings. The handle, chip and phone contact stay clear.
D02-1 uses the D01 ST2 phone mark, unplugged, with PROP-07 in ST1. Now that the work zone carries no marks, no wipe or reset is needed.
The front faces 235° in every state, so nobody turns the dripper in the hand.
The phone bumper has 1.5 mm corner pads and open edges, which gives the D01-B4b glow a physical path. A leak of 5-15 mm is ASSUMED until the glow test. The rings carry the turn.
PROP-01's look is ASSUMED: a size-02 handle-less cone, cream satin glaze pooling to gloss, a raw foot and no exterior mark. Every hex and contrast figure depends on it.
Contrast ratios are WCAG relative luminance, computed from the stated hexes under an even key (18% grey card #767676). Light direction, phone light balance and gloss highlights are DP requests.
Some dressing is not named in the script: the charging cable and grommet, the rack contents and TILE-01. The filter is binned and the kettle returned off-screen between beats.

Every cross-reference is keyed to the script's scene_ids (S1-S4) and beat_ids (D01-B1 to D01-B6, D02-1, D02-2). No shot or sound IDs from other departments are cited, since none is in this department's upstream.

No reference imagery was supplied or inspected, and no reference_reader tool is bound in this run. Only the verified facts are relied on. The set makes no performance claims and shows no price or award cards.
sources: Brief PROJECT_001: verified product facts 'Hand-glazed stoneware ceramic', 'Dishwasher safe', 'Made in small batches'; must-include and must-avoid lists; tone 'quiet, warm, tactile'

Script beat_sheet S1-S4 and D01 beats D01-B1 to D01-B6, stills D02-1 and D02-2, and the script decisions (filter and grounds go in during the D01-B2/D01-B3 cut; finger pads in D01-B4b; no drips on the outer glaze; the phone stays face-down in D01-B5 to D01-B6)
Route R1 product_role and visual_language (terracotta, cream, soft grey; sound over music)
Studio taste notes: 'One real detail per scene', 'The product is a tool, then a hero', 'Real kitchens have a dish rack and a charging cable', and the window-and-mug reject
Production Designer craft brief: plan with numbers, specified palettes, product job and 3:1 backing, mirror paths, continuity keyed to beat_ids, blank surfaces

blockers.issue: The D01-B4b edge glow on the bumper case has not been measured. The 5-15 mm leak on all four open edges is ASSUMED.
blockers.resolution: Before the shoot day, with the DP: shoot the case face-down at 230.0/302.8 on a #533C2B sample board with the lock screen lit, under the D01-B4b lighting, and publish which edges leak and how far. The edge touching the mug will likely leak least. D01-B4b does not depend on this, because the rings carry the turn.

blockers.issue: The grommet route, OUT-01 below the top, TILE-01's coffee mirror line, CEIL-01's extent and the glaze pool's mirror paths have been checked in plan and section only, not on a monitor.
blockers.resolution: At prelight, with the DP, confirm on the monitor that: (1) the D01-B2 card area, D01-B4a to D01-B4b, D01-B5 to D01-B6 and D02-2 show no outlet or cable; (2) the D01-B4b coffee shows paint and TILE-01's 112 cm edge where the published line puts it, and the rings bend that edge; (3) in D01-B5 to D01-B6 and D02-2 the pool sees only oak, flats, CEIL-01, TILE-01 and the WIN-01 diffusion, with no lamp opening, studio or crew beyond the lens flag; (4) TILE-01 never backs the dripper's outline; (5) D01-B2's first angle stays on the wall-C side of y 185, or FAUCET-01 gets built. If the plug end shows in D01-B5 to D01-B6, swap to a right-angle USB-C plug turned toward wall C within 1.5 cm of the port and republish the route. If anything beyond the WIN-01 diffusion shows in a reflection, reinstate the translight with its rights clearance.

blockers.issue: The script's sound lines for D01-B2, D01-B4b, D01-B5 and D01-B6 call for kitchen room tone and the kettle ticking as it cools. LOC-01 is a stage build, so stage tone is not kitchen tone.
blockers.resolution: Record wild room tone, and the cooling ticks of an enamel stovetop kettle, in a real pre-war US rental kitchen, with the kettle placed as RANGE-01 is (about 1.8 m toward wall A from the dripper). Or confirm that stage tone is acceptable.

blockers.issue: PROP-01 is invented: its shape, size, glaze colourway, raw foot and lack of a stamp are all ASSUMED. Every hex and contrast figure, the swap test and D02-2 (the DTC product image) depend on it. Pending item: the client's product reference (photos or CAD of the shipping glaze, the foot finish and any stamp). Source: Solace Home Goods. Owner: producer.
blockers.resolution: Get the reference before PROP-01 is locked and before D02-2 is generated; work can continue on the ASSUMED spec until then. When it arrives, re-run the 3:1 checks against the #533C2B oak and the #6B6E67 paint, and repaint the walls lighter if the glaze's relative luminance is below 0.2. If the foot is glazed, the raw band's 2.9:1 separation on the mug goes: re-solve the seat and keep the glaze pool as the swap test. Any stamp stays on the underside.

evidence.specificity: All six prior notes are addressed, and the page is a build document with numbers that check out. "PROP-02 phone: long axis along x, top toward 90°, port at the aisle end. ST1 is face-up at 230.0/304.8 ... ST2-ST4 is face-down at 230.0/302.8 (case x 222.3-237.7, y 299.0-306.6), its mug-side edge touching the mug at 232.7/299". The coffee mirror line is published and correct: "TILE-01's 112.0 cm edge lands mid-coffee at h = 98.5 + 0.494·d: 118.3 cm at d 40, 123.2 at d 50, 128.2 at d 60". A stylist, builder, DP or generator can act on almost every line without asking. Two things keep it off 10. First, PROP-01's entrance in the rack has no stated backing or ratio. Second, PROP-05's filter numbers ("about Ø 9 cm at the mouth") cannot produce the "1.0 cm collar above the rim" on an 11.5 cm rim, so the stylist would have to ask which is right.
evidence.distinctiveness: The set exists because of this script and this product. "The thickest 4 cm arc of that pool is the 'front': the mark her thumb crosses in D01-B2 and the only swap-test detail". "S3: the coffee rings bending TILE-01's reflected edge, with the phone against the mug". "The phone charged on this counter overnight, not by her bed (PROP-08)". The tile course exists only to give the rings an edge to bend, and the phone-against-mug geometry exists only because the buzz has to reach the cup. It stops short of 9 for two reasons: a pooled glaze foot is a common trait of handmade ceramic cones, and the landlord kitchen around it (grey-green paint, a dish rack, butcher block) is well made but belongs to the category.
evidence.fit: The two fit problems from the last round are fixed. "Mark 1, Mark 1b and the secondary swap test are cut ... 232.7/280 is clean oak in every state, and the glaze pool, which rests on the verified 'hand-glazed', is the only swap test." And: "No filter is on the counter before D01-B3 ... 'Started the ritual before the phone lit' contradicted the S1 turn". The closing product moment is now readable by number: "Body #E3D9C6 on the oak #533C2B: 7.3:1 ... the pool is 3.8:1 and the raw flange edge #A88663 is 3.1:1". The set follows the taste notes ("The rack, mug and cable are texture ('Real kitchens have a dish rack and a charging cable')", "The window is never in frame, and nobody looks out of it") and states only verified facts. Two gaps hold it at 8. The product's first appearance, the lift from the rack, has no designed separation. And the cable's back run lands in the closing hold, the frame the must-include "readable closing product moment" depends on.
evidence.craft: I recomputed the published ratios with WCAG relative luminance and they hold: body on oak 7.32, pool 3.82, flange 3.05, raw band on the mug 2.92, bumper 2.22, cable 1.37, tile on paint 3.60. The section path is also correct: "0° to 32.8°: the wall-B flat at y ≈ 117, 92-275 cm" (a 284 cm run with a 183 cm rise), and "wall D from 275 cm down to 92 + 33.3·tan θ cm". Screen direction is solved in plan: "the rack lies at frame right of the mug as seen from the aisle, so the D01-B2 carry runs right to left". Every state is keyed to script IDs ("ST4 (D01-B4a to D01-B4b, not before D01-B3)"). Three slips a senior would catch keep it at 8. (1) PROP-04 puts the cream product among #D6D4CD wire, a #BFC0BA tray and a #F2EFE8 plate "stood in the wall-D slots", which is 1.06-1.3:1 with no separation. (2) The PROP-08 run along y 322 to the grommet at 258/322 sits inside the D01-B5/B6 frame behind the phone, which contradicts "PROP-08 is plugged in, off frame". (3) A Ø 9 cm filter mouth cannot collar an 11.5 cm rim.

notes.note: Give the product's entrance a separation you control, and publish its ratios. In D01-B2's first angle the #E3D9C6 body stands in #D6D4CD white wire (1.06:1) on a #BFC0BA tray (1.3:1). The #F2EFE8 plate "stood in the wall-D slots" sits directly behind the dripper as seen from the aisle (1.2:1). The glaze pool the thumb crosses reads 2.3:1 on the plate and 1.8:1 on the wire. Every other PROP-01 state has published ratios; this one has none. Fix it inside the rack. Re-spec the wire as black matte epoxy (for example #2A2C2E) on a charcoal tray. Strike the plate, or move it to the wall-A end of the rack (slots at y 190-200) so nothing pale stands between 232.7/213 and wall D. The body then reads about 10:1 on the wire and 3.7:1 on the #6B6E67 backsplash, and the pool about 5.2:1 on the wire. Add these ST1 figures to product_placement. Keep the dry, sponge-free dressing and the rationale that goes with it.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'At least 3:1 relative-luminance contrast between the backing and the part of the product doing the job ... Tone-on-tone needs a separation you control'. Script decision: the B2/B3 cut 'gives the product's first appearance time to land'. Brief must-include: 'A clear product role in the story'.

notes.target: spatial_layout PROP-08 route, OUT-01 and grommet paragraphs; PROP-08 ST1-ST2; LOC-01 frame lock 'D01-B5 to D01-B6: 02 only. PROP-08 is plugged in, off frame'; blocker 2
notes.note: Reroute the cable so the closing hold is clean. With the pool's front at 235°, the planned hero view runs along 55° through 232.7/280. From there the grommet at 258/322 sits about 20 cm left of that axis and 45 cm beyond the dripper. That is the same lateral offset as the phone's inner corner (237.7/306.6: about 19 cm left, 19 cm beyond), and the script puts that corner 'at the frame edge'. So the y 322 run from x ≈ 235 to 258 and the grommet ring fall inside the D01-B5/B6 frame, and blocker 2's right-angle-plug fallback only covers the port end. Move the grommet into the end strip against wall C, directly under the loop (about 216/334), and move OUT-01 to the wall-C end inside the base cabinet. The route becomes port → x 218 → loop → grommet and never runs toward wall D. At 216/334 it sits about 54 cm left of the hero axis. Republish PROP-08 ST1/ST2 and the 'never enters' rule. In the same pass, add to prelight item (3) a check that the WIN-01 opening stays out of the D01-B5/B6 and D02-2 frames, because its jamb at x 250 is only 10 cm from the C/D corner the hero axis aims at.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Continuity is position and state' and 'Put marks where a planned view sees them'. Brief must-include: 'A readable closing product moment'. Quality bar craft: 'continuity that holds'.

notes.target: PROP-05 description ('Opened, a filter is about Ø 9 cm at the mouth and about 10 cm long') and ST2-ST4; product_placement 'the bloom in the white filter is 13.8:1'; PROP-02 ST3 'ticking against the mug on its corner pad'
notes.note: Fix three physical slips. (1) A Ø 9 cm mouth sits inside PROP-01's Ø 11.5 cm rim (inner diameter about 10.5-11 cm), so the '1.0 cm collar above the rim' in ST2-ST4 cannot happen. Re-size the filter to a paper that opens wider than the rim (a size-02 cone paper opens to roughly Ø 13 cm, ASSUMED). State the rim's wall thickness so the collar height repeats between takes and runs. (2) ST4 darkens the paper to #B09A7C up to 1 cm below the rim, so the bloom #2E1E14 reads on wet paper at about 5.9:1, not 13.8:1 on dry #F1EEE6. Correct the figure. (3) The mug contact at 232.7/299 is on the bumper's long side wall, 5 cm from the 237.7 corner, not on a corner pad. The pads face the oak. Say which surface ticks.
notes.source: Quality bar craft: 'nothing physically implausible'. Craft brief: 'two generation runs must get the same room from it'.

notes.target: spatial_layout NOT BUILT list ('Any frame that shows y < 185 needs FAUCET-01 built') and blocker 2 item (5)
notes.note: Build FAUCET-01 now; don't leave it conditional. The rack's y 190 edge is 5 cm from the sink cut-out (y 125-185). The D01-B1 hand exits toward that spot, and D01-B2's first angle lifts from it, so a built, dry sink with no tap is one reframe away from reading as a set. Spec it at 254/155 with a spout height that clears the upper cabinets at 145 cm. Give it a matte finish (for example matte black powder-coat, not polished chrome, which reflects about 60% and would add a mirror path next to the rack). Keep the body blank and add FAUCET-01 to the blank-surfaces list. Mark 3 at 204/185 then has a working sink to belong to.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Shiny parts show their mirror path' and 'Generators add fake logos ... list the surfaces that must stay blank'. CD reject: 'A room nobody has lived in'. Taste notes: 'Real kitchens have a dish rack and a charging cable'.

notes.target: palette entry 3 ('#F2EFE8 white gloss glaze ... and #D5D8D2 pale sage-grey matte tile ... Neutral, 9%') and palette entry 1 (oak sample)
notes.note: Give TILE-01 its own share. It is a different hex, material and finish from the glazes and the crepe paper, and it is a visible band in D01-B4b, D01-B5/B6 and D02-2. Split its share out inside entry 3 (for example 'tile x% of the 9%'), or give it its own entry and move the 1% cable into a note to stay at six. Also give the oak sample a tolerance. The raw flange clears 3:1 only just (3.05:1 on #533C2B), and the bible itself says #5A4230 drops it to 2.8:1. Write the sample spec as 'matches #533C2B or darker under the 18% card, never lighter', so a warm sample board can't sink the D02-2 foot below 3:1.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Each entry is a hex, a role ..., the material and finish that carry it, and its share of the master view' and 'At least 3:1'. Brief must-include: 'A readable closing product moment'.

keep: The glaze pool as the only swap test: 'The thickest 4 cm arc of that pool is the front', crossed by the thumb in D01-B2 and facing 235° in every state, never turned in the hand.
232.7/280 is clean oak in every state, and 'No paid image shows a mark the product made'.
The #533C2B tinted-hardwax oak, the #77756F bumper and the published WCAG ratios (body 7.3:1, pool 3.8:1, raw band on the mug 2.9:1). They check out by recomputation.
TILE-01 as the one designed edge for the coffee to bend, with the published mirror line 'h = 98.5 + 0.494·d', the 31-149° bearing window and the rule that it never backs the dripper's outline.
The section-and-plan mirror path for the pool, with CEIL-01 and full-height flats on walls A, B and C.
The phone-mug-dripper geometry: the phone's mug-side edge touching the mug at 232.7/299, the set-down at 232.7/280 and 'phone, mug, dripper' in a line along y.
Screen direction solved in plan, with the rack at frame right, so the D01-B2 carry runs right to left.

The history told by objects: PROP-03's tide line 2 cm below the rim as the S1 detail, the chip at 195° from FAUCET-01, the kettle's scorch band from RANGE-01's front burner, and Mark 2's forearm wear.
PROP-05 held in the upper cabinet until the D01-B2/D01-B3 cut, with no filter, canister, spoon or box in any frame.
Frame locks of at most 5 props, the blank-surfaces list, and the composited lock-screen spec ('7:00' #1B1F24 on #E4E7EA, a glyphless banner).
The dry rack dressing and its reasoning against D02-2's dishwasher line.
Blocker 4: the product reference is pending with the producer, sourced from Solace Home Goods, with the re-check steps spelled out.
Every state keyed to the script's full beat_ids ('not before D01-B2'), with no invented shot or sound IDs.

scenes.performance_beats:
NORA's scene. Hero beat: B1 (SH01), close on the flip. She moves at habit pace from her first frame (casting). The only urgency belongs to the phone, and it ends at the flip.

B1 (0.0-1.5, SH01). Objective: get the coffee going before the day gets anything. Obstacle: PROP-02 is lit at 7:00 and buzzing beside her mug. Action: R lands on it without slowing, turns it face-down so it settles against the mug, and carries on toward the rack in one move, with no pause and no glance. Real detail: she flips it while it is still plugged in. It charged here overnight (PROP-08), and she doesn't unplug it to refuse it. The tide line inside the empty mug (the world bible's S1 detail) reads in the same frame.

B2 (1.5-4.5, SH02A + SH02B). Objective: get the dripper on the mug before the kettle is ready. Obstacle: the dripper is drying in the rack, 82 cm from the mug. Action: R takes PROP-01 the way she'd take an empty cup. Index and middle fingers hook over the near rim into the dry cone, with the thumb outside. As the grip closes, the thumb lands at the foot and draws up the front across the glaze pool without stopping (script). She carries it low and level, seats it on the mug with a click, lets go and leaves it there, with the hand clear of the phone. Filter and grounds go in during the B2/B3 cut (script).

Hands: R does every action in S1. L hangs at her side through the rack trip, which falls in the cuts. From SH02B's first frame, L lies flat on the front edge at y≈320, off frame.
Entry: NORA at N2, both hands at her sides. PROP-02 ST1, PROP-08 ST1, PROP-03 ST1 (empty, tide line visible), PROP-04 ST1, PROP-01 ST1 (dry, in the rack, front at 235°). PROP-05 is in the upper cabinet. PROP-06 is heating off-set.
Exit: PROP-01 and PROP-03 at ST2 (empty dripper seated). PROP-04 ST2. PROP-02 and PROP-08 at ST2 (face-down, touching the mug, still plugged in). R has gone toward wall A. L lies flat at y≈320.
scenes.blocking:
Only her hand and forearm are seen. The prop marks are the world bible's. NORA's marks are mine, worked out from reach.

N2 (start and return): centred at y 308, hips 2 cm off the front edge (x≈195), facing 90°. Chest at y 289-327; right shoulder at about 185/293, 137 cm up (ASSUMED).
Rack mark: centred at y 215 (chest at y 196-234, right shoulder at about 185/196). From here the dripper's near side is at about 250°, inside the front's thick arc (about 201-269°), so the rim hook puts her thumb on the front without turning the dripper. The trip N2 → rack mark → N2 falls inside the two elliptical cuts, so no frame shows her stepping.

Line of action along the counter:
- Out, toward wall A: R leaves the phone, passes the mug and goes to the rack.
- Back, the opposite way: R carries the dripper toward wall C along the x 232.7 strip, foot 12 ±2 cm over the oak, to the mug (232.7/295).
- After the seat: R withdraws back along the carry line toward wall A, where the filters are kept, and never passes over the phone.

Frames. Every lens is in the aisle on the wall-A side, looking past her right flank, so her torso is never in frame.
- SH01 (55°): about 34 cm across at the phone, rack out (ruling 1). It holds PROP-02, the mug with its tide line, and PROP-08 wherever it shows (lock 02/03/08). The sightline passes x 195 at y 280, 9 cm off her flank. R exits frame right, toward the rack.
- SH02A (25°, on the rack): about 40 cm across, with a fallback of about 25 cm (see flags). The front is 30° off the lens, so the thumb crosses the pool on the lens side, left of centre. R enters from frame left. On plan, her nearest torso corner is about 27 cm left of the line to the dripper and 31 cm nearer the lens, which is outside the frame (Cinematographer to confirm, blocker 1).
- SH02B (55°), with NORA back at N2: it holds PROP-01, PROP-03, PROP-02 touching the mug, and PROP-08 wherever it shows. The dripper travels right to left.

Card 'Nobody gets you before the pour.': in at 1.5 s on the SH01/SH02A cut and out at 4.5 s, across both angles (script). World position: the card area the world bible keeps bare on the wall-D paint (125 cm up and above, y 240-340), in the upper third of both frames. In SH02A it sits above the rim, clear of the thumb's whole path from foot to rim band. In SH02B it sits above the carry, where the dripper and hand stay below about 115 cm. D01 is native 9:16, so nothing is cropped.
scenes.action_progression:
SH01, B1 (0.0-1.5):
- 0.0-0.8: PROP-02 lies face-up with '7:00' and the banner lit, buzzing in its footprint. The eye is on '7:00'.
- 0.8-1.2: R lands without slowing (ruling 9): thumb on the wall-C long edge, fingertips on the mug-side edge. It lifts the phone 2 cm, turns it over its long axis toward the mug and lets go 1 cm above the oak. The phone lands face-down 2 cm nearer the mug, with its mug-side edge against the mug. Knock; the buzz ends (PROP-02 and PROP-08 to ST2).
- 1.2-1.5: R lifts off toward wall A and exits frame right past the mug.
Elliptical cut at 1.5 s, and the card comes in.

SH02A, B2 first angle (1.50-2.25, 18 f):
- f1-6 (1.50-1.75): R arrives over the rack's aisle-side wires. Index and middle fingers hook the near rim. The thumb lands at the foot on the front and, as the grip closes, sweeps up across the pool to the rim band without stopping.
- f7-14 (1.75-2.08): R lifts the dripper about 14 cm straight up until the foot clears the 13 cm wires. Faint knock off the tray (PROP-01 and PROP-04 to ST2).
- f15-18 (2.08-2.25): R sets off toward wall C, level, for about 5 cm.
Elliptical cut mid-carry at 2.25 s (script). About 65 cm of the carry falls in the cut.

SH02B, B2 second angle (2.25-4.50, 54 f):
- f1-10: opens with the dripper in the right third, 12 cm short of the mug with its foot 12 cm over the oak, already moving right to left. It carries 12 cm.
- f11-15: R lowers it the last 2.5 cm onto the rim. Click on f15.
- f16-20: the fingers unhook, the thumb comes off, and R rises 3 cm.
- f21-30: R withdraws along the carry line toward wall A and exits frame right.
- f31-54: the empty dripper sits on the mug, and the mug still touches the phone. Nothing moves.

1.5 + 0.75 + 2.25 = 4.5 s, and every shot is under 5 s. SH02A's 18 f stand (ruling 6), because SH02B's f15 seat is the product's first full look. Peak hand speed is about 0.6 m/s or below.
scenes.emotional_shift:
NORA holds. Her hand moves at one speed onto the phone and off it, because a visible decision would be acting (casting). The shift belongs to the frame.
- Before: the phone is face-up, lit and buzzing. The day asks first.
- Trigger: her hand lands on it at 0.8 s.
- After: by 1.2 s the screen is down, dark and silent, and the same hand is already moving at the same speed toward the dripper.
The dripper plays no part in the trigger, so nothing credits it with calming her. The flip leaves the phone touching her mug, which B4b pays off.
scenes.transition_in: Cold open, hard in on frame 1. The phone is already lit and the buzz starts on frame 1, with no fade. The eye sits on '7:00' until R arrives at 0.8 s.
scenes.transition_out:
1.5 s, SH01 to SH02A: an elliptical cut on direction (ruling 2). R exits SH01 frame right and enters SH02A from frame left onto the dripper, so screen travel stays left to right and the trip to the rack falls in the cut. The eye goes from the hand leaving past the mug (right third) to the hand landing on the rim (left of centre). The card comes in on this cut. Silence crosses it, because the knock ended at 1.2 s.

2.25 s, SH02A to SH02B: an elliptical cut mid-carry (script). The dripper moves right to left on both axes at the same height over the oak. The eye stays on the dripper as it goes from centre to the right third. The card holds, and room tone crosses.

4.5 s, out to S2: a same-axis cut-in on 55°, across the ellipsis in which the filter and grounds go in. PROP-01 on PROP-03 carries across. The eye goes from the empty dripper on the mug to the heaped grounds at SH03's centre. The card ends on the cut, and room tone crosses it.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'Before the phone, the inbox, or anyone else gets a piece of you, there are five minutes that are only yours — marked by the pour.' Carried by the B1 flip of PROP-02 (SH01) and by the same R taking PROP-01 in B2, with the thumb crossing its glaze pool (SH02A). Cut this and the viewer loses the choice itself: the phone refused at 7:00 and the dripper taken instead. They also lose the phone left against her mug, which B4b needs, and the first touch of the mark that B5 names as 'Hand-glazed stoneware.'
practical_or_compositing_flags: SH01 legible screen text. Method: composite on the practical plate. The real phone shows a flat #E4E7EA field, so its light on the oak and her hand is real. Acceptance: in the 34 cm rack-out frame, with the digits about 35° off upright, '7:00' reads on a 6-inch phone at 100% from 0.0 to 0.8 s. The banner's two lines stay unreadable. There is no other glyph, status bar or logo, and the digits stay locked to the glass until the phone goes edge-on at about 1.0 s. Risk: an unreadable '7:00' costs the hook and the 7:05 payoff.

SH01 flip, the hero beat. It combines finger work, a turn in the air, a live cable and contact with the mug. Method: practical plate with a hand double matched to NORA's anchors (release pending, blocker 7). Acceptance: the grip is as ruled, turned in one continuous 0.4 s move. The phone lands face-down at 230.0/302.8, touching the mug, and the mug stays on 232.7/295. The cable stays in the port and its loop rolls to ST2. The R mole reads, and the hand's speed is the same before and after. The knock is the real case on the real oak. Risk: a gap between the phone and the mug leaves B4b's rings no path. Retake it; don't fix it in post.

SH02A thumb pass and lift. This is a hand on the product doing fine finger work, and it is the first sight of the glaze pool that later carries 'hand-glazed' (claim_demo_needs_clearance, with SH06 and SH08). Method: practical on the real unit with the hand double. The fallback is a pickup, not generation (ruling 10). At the prelight the PD confirms that the rack's aisle-side wires leave the thumb a clear path to the foot (about 8 cm on plan). Acceptance: on a 6-inch phone at 100%, with the card on, the thumb visibly lands on the foot and sweeps up over the pool without stopping, on the lens side of the front's thick arc. Glaze shows on both sides of the hand. The front stays at 235° and is never turned. The foot clears the wires with one faint knock. If the sweep doesn't read at about 40 cm, SH02A tightens to about 25 cm, which also keeps her torso further out. If the card still pulls the eye off the thumb, see blocker 5. Risk: a thumb that misses the arc, or doesn't read, loses B5's setup, and one that stops reads as a caress for the camera.

SH02B carry and seat, with hands on the product. Method: practical on the real unit. Acceptance: the dripper travels level at 12 ±2 cm over the oak and never drops below the mug's 9.5 cm rim height until it is over the mug. It is lowered 2.5 cm onto the rim in one move, with the click on f15 and the raw band hanging 2 mm outside the rim. The front stays at 235°. The hand leaves toward wall A and never passes over the phone, and the phone still touches the mug afterwards. The click is the real unit on the real mug, not sweetened. Risk: a dip-and-pop carry reads as fake, and a nudged phone breaks B4b.

Bodies in SH01 to SH02B. Method: practical, with the double's feet on the taped N2 and rack marks and every take checked on the monitor. Acceptance: her torso, upper arm and L never enter SH01, SH02A (at either frame size) or SH02B. Risk: a hip or shoulder at the frame edge breaks the hands-only casting.

scenes.performance_beats:
NORA's scene, played by her left hand off frame. Hero beat: B3 (SH03), close on the stream meeting the grounds.

B3 (4.5-7.0). Objective: start the bloom from the centre out without the stream touching the paper. Obstacle: water that hits the paper runs down past the coffee. Action: L brings PROP-06 in by its beech loop handle, with the forearm still and only the wrist circling (casting). The stream makes two circuits, from the centre out to a finger's width short of the paper and back. Then she stops it clean and the spout lifts out. Only the spout is in frame (script).

Deliberate break of the taste note 'One real detail per scene': D01-B3 carries the pour alone, and S2's detail, the kettle's scorch band, moves to D02-1 (SH07). The reason: SH03's frame is about 20 cm wide, and the kettle body sits 14-27 cm frame-left of the cone, so holding the band would halve the bloom. The script makes the same choice.

Hands (restaged): L pours. The handle is on her left, so L takes it from her left shoulder with a natural grip and no cross. From this kettle position R would have to pour cross-body with a backhand grip. R hangs at her side, off frame, in B3 and D02-1. Nothing touches the product while it performs.
Entry, after the ellipsis: L holds PROP-06 just off frame-left, with the spout not yet in, and R is at her side. PROP-05 ST3 (dry heap, peak 3.0 cm below the rim). PROP-01 ST3 on PROP-03. PROP-02 ST2. PROP-08 ST2, plugged in, off frame.
Exit: L and the kettle are out frame-left. PROP-05 ST4 (bloomed). PROP-03 ST3 (coffee rising, light steam).
Everything plays at 100% speed (taste reject: slow motion used to make something look expensive).
scenes.blocking:
NORA stands at N2, facing 90°. Her left shoulder is at about 185/323.

Kettle at the pour: the body is centred at about 220/311, level with the cone in depth. The spout runs toward about 140°, square to the lens, so it reads in profile. The handle is at about 215/317, 9 cm to her left of midline. L reaches it about 31 cm forward and slightly right of her left shoulder, with no cross and no lean. The spout tip sits 1-3 cm over the rim at the cone centre (232.7/295). The kettle comes in along the spout's line from about 7 cm back and leaves the same way, then goes off frame toward the aisle and the burner (212/97). The stream stays inside the cone.

SH03 (55°, about 20 cm across): the sightline to the cone passes x 195 at y≈269, 20 cm clear of her. In frame: the spout entering from frame left, the stream, the cone, the mug, and the phone's dark face-down wall-D end at lower left (ruling 3; continuity with SH02B and SH04). Out of frame-left: the kettle body, the scorch band, L, R, the phone's port end and PROP-08 (lock: PROP-02's wall-D end, 03, 05, 06). The 'bottom edge above the counter' requirement and its paint-out fallback are withdrawn.

D02-1 (SH07): same marks at the same moment, on a separate 4:5 plate staged wider. It is not a crop of SH03. L's fingers on the beech handle show at the top-left corner, cropped to include the index finger's middle joint so the scar reads. This is the one exception to 'L never in frame'. In frame: the kettle body with its scorch band, the stream landing on the bloom, the whole dripper, the mug, and PROP-02 face-down, dark and unplugged against the mug. PROP-08 is struck, and 232.7/280 is clean oak.
scenes.action_progression:
SH03, B3 (4.5-7.0), one uncut take of 60 f:
- 4.5-4.7: the heaped grounds sit alone at frame centre, still.
- 4.7-4.9: the spout comes in from frame left along its own line and stops over the peak.
- 4.9-6.5: L tips the kettle, and a thin stream lands on the peak. It makes two circuits, from the centre out to a finger's width short of the paper and back. The grounds darken outward from the centre and start to rise (PROP-05 ST3 to ST4).
- 6.5-6.7: L tips back, the stream stops clean, and the spout lifts out frame-left.
- 6.7-7.0: the bloom holds alone, still fizzing.

One pass mark for every take: by 6.7 s the whole visible bed has darkened, and the centre has risen enough to see on a 6-inch phone at 100%. The minimum is about 5 mm, and about 1 cm is the target, not the pass. The grounds bloom on screen for 2.1 s, inside the route's 2-3 s hold. The take starts and ends on a holdable state (the heap alone; the bloom alone). SH07 captures the moment at about 5.7 s: the second outward circuit landing on the bloom.
scenes.emotional_shift: Hold. No trigger arrives, and none should: her wrist keeps one pace from the first drop to the last. The only change is physical, from a dry heap to a bloom. A visible reaction to the bloom would claim that the dripper relaxes her, which is an unverified benefit.
scenes.transition_in: A same-axis cut-in on 55° from SH02B, across the ellipsis in which the filter and grounds go in. The grounds are already heaped in a pressed filter (script). The eye goes from the empty dripper on the mug to the heap at frame centre, and the spout arrives there 0.2 s later. Room tone crosses the cut, and the first new sound is the stream at 4.9 s.
scenes.transition_out: A hard cut at 7.0 s on the same 55° axis, widening to SH04 across the 'MOMENTS LATER' ellipsis (the drawdown, and the kettle going back to its burner). PROP-01 on PROP-03 carries across. The eye goes from the bloom at frame centre to the dripper on the mug, with R already in its grip. The fizz stops dead on the cut, and room tone marks the time passing. The first new sound is the last drip, at about 7.25 s.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'Before the phone, the inbox, or anyone else gets a piece of you, there are five minutes that are only yours — marked by the pour.' Carried by B3 (SH03): the PROP-06 stream spiralling into PROP-01 and the grounds blooming inside it. Cut this and the viewer loses the pour that marks the five minutes, and the dripper never works on screen. The spot would jump from refusing the phone to a finished cup, with no tool before the hero (taste note).
practical_or_compositing_flags: SH03 stream and bloom, which are the product's own output. Method: practical only, on the real unit with real water and coffee at 100% speed. There is no generated fallback. Acceptance: one thin, continuous stream from the 5 mm spout that lands only on the grounds, never on the paper. The take meets the single pass mark (whole visible bed darkened, centre visibly risen by at least about 5 mm by 6.7 s, on a 6-inch phone at 100%). The paper darkens no higher than 1 cm below the rim, the collar stays dry, and nothing overflows. No speed ramp, and no foam, bubbles or steam added in post. A take below the pass mark is not used. If no take passes, blocker 3's fix applies. Risk: a ramped or over-foamed bloom overstates what the dripper does.

SH03 and SH07 left-hand pour (restaged). Method: practical, with the hand double pouring left-handed. It is rehearsed at the prelight, after casting's left-hand test. Acceptance: the forearm stays still and only the wrist circles, and the stream never wobbles or gets corrected. R never enters either frame. In SH07 the L scar reads at the index finger's middle joint, and no mole shows. Risk: an unsteady pour with her weaker hand reads as unpractised and breaks casting's years-of-habit read. The wrong anchor on the pouring hand breaks continuity.

SH03 frame contents. Method: framing (the Cinematographer's). The PD supplies PROP-06 and PROP-03 unmarked. Acceptance: the phone's wall-D end reads dark at lower left. No port, cable, kettle body, scorch band or hand is in frame, and no text or mark shows on the spout or the mug. Risk: a stray cable, glow or invented brand pulls the eye off the bloom.

SH07 (D02-1) still: liquids, with a hand on the kettle. Method: practical, with the stream frozen by the exposure. The hand-double release is pending (blocker 7). Acceptance: L's fingers on the beech handle at the top-left corner. The 1 cm scorch band (#6E3A2A) reads at the kettle base. The stream lands on the bloom, and the dripper is whole and unobstructed. The phone lies face-down, dark and unplugged against the mug, and PROP-08 is struck. Copy space stays clear of the dripper, the kettle and the pour. Risk: a split stream, a splash on the outer glaze, or a scorch band cleaned off, which would lose S2's detail.

scenes.performance_beats:
NORA's scene. Hero beat: B4b (SH05), with her hand, the coffee surface and the phone in one frame.

B4a (7.0-8.5, SH04). Objective: get the dripper off the mug without dripping on the oak. Obstacle: a last drop is hanging at the exit hole. Action: R lifts PROP-01 3 cm and holds it over the coffee until the drop falls, and the drop ends the hold. Then, in one arc, R carries it 15 cm toward wall A and sets it on the oak just past the mug, away from the phone, which uncovers the coffee. Grip: a claw over the rim, with the fingertips on the outer glaze under the rim band and the palm clear of the spent filter's collar. Real detail: she waits out the last drip over the mug instead of carrying a dripping cone.

B4b (8.5-11.5, SH05). Objective: take her coffee as soon as it is cool enough to hold. Obstacle: it is too hot to grip, and the phone rattles against it. Action: the heel of R rests on the oak in front of the mug. The fingertips run along the mug's aisle side below the rim, with the palm clear and the thumb along the index, so the hand touches the mug without gripping it. When the phone rattles and rings run through the coffee, nothing in the hand moves: no flinch, no squeeze and no drift toward the phone. The rattle stops, the rings flatten, and her hand stays where it is (script). Real detail: fingertips on a just-brewed mug with the palm held off it, which is how she waits every morning. Scene detail: the rings bending TILE-01's reflected edge (script, world bible).

Entry, after the ellipsis: R in its claw on PROP-01, still. PROP-01 on PROP-03, with PROP-05 ST5 in the cone and a drop hanging (blocker 4). PROP-03 ST4. PROP-02 ST2, touching the mug. PROP-08 ST2. PROP-06 is on its burner, off frame. L lies flat on the front edge at y≈320, off frame.
Exit: R still on the mug. PROP-01 ST4 on 232.7/280, with the spent filter in. PROP-02 dark and back against the mug. The coffee is flat.
scenes.blocking:
NORA stands at N2: centred at y 308, hips 2 cm off the edge, facing 90°, right shoulder at about 185/293. Only R crosses the front edge, and only between y≈280 and y≈300. L rests flat at y 315-325.

B4a: R lifts PROP-01 3 cm straight up off PROP-03 (232.7/295). It carries the dripper 15 cm toward wall A along the x 232.7 strip, with the foot clearing the rim before it descends, and sets it on clean oak at 232.7/280 (±1 cm), front at 235°. The phone, the mug and the dripper now sit in a line.
B4b: R comes about 15 cm back toward wall C, opposite the way it went out, and settles. The heel sits on the oak at about 225.7/295, 3 cm in front of the mug and at least 2 cm clear of the case (y ≥299). The pads rest over 225-315° below the rim, with the thumb inside 315°. The handle (90°), the chip (195°) and the phone contact (0°) stay clear. The arm is nearly straight, with light weight on the heel and no lean. Her wrist crossing the phone's port end in frame is accepted (ruling 5).

Frames:
- SH04 and SH05, the plan of record as one take: 55°, from the aisle past her right flank, about 42 cm across at the dripper's plane, 1.7x SH06. The sightlines pass x 195 at y≈254 (to 280) and y≈269 (to the mug). The frame holds the dripper at 280, the coffee surface (the view must see into the mug once B4a uncovers it), all of PROP-02, PROP-05 in the cone, and PROP-08 wherever it shows (lock 02/03/05/08). The rack's wall-C corner (220/236) is about 29 cm frame-right of the line to 280, so it stays out, and so does WIN-01.
- SH05 reframed, only if blocker 2 fails at 42 cm: about 30 cm across, on a bearing between 31° and 55° so TILE-01 stays in the coffee's mirror path (world bible). The dripper, mug and phone stack up the 9:16 frame instead of running across it, and the dripper stays in frame for the whole beat (script). Her torso stays out: at 40°, the sightline to the mug passes x 195 at y≈250. SH04 then cuts to SH05 at the settle (ruling 4 reopened).

The card 'Everyone else gets you at 7:05.' sits in the world bible's bare card area (wall-D paint, 125 cm up and above, y 240-340), clear of the dripper, the coffee and the hand.
scenes.action_progression:
SH04-SH05 is one locked practical take from 7.0 to 11.5 s: 108 f, under 5 s (ruling 4). The drop, the settle and the rings are live events, so the beat runs on cues, not the clock, and the still-hand tail absorbs the drift.

SH04, B4a (nominal 7.00-8.50, 36 f):
- 7.00-7.17 (4 f): R lifts PROP-01 3 cm off the rim and holds it level.
- 7.17-7.33 (4 f nominal): the hanging drop falls into the coffee: plink. The drop ends the hold. Accepted window: 7.17-7.42.
- 7.33-7.75 (10 f): 2 f after the drop, R carries the dripper in one arc 15 cm toward wall A, clear of the rim, down onto 232.7/280: stoneware on wood (PROP-01 ST4, PROP-07 ST2).
- 7.75-8.00 (6 f): release. The fingertips open off the outer glaze, and R rises 2 cm clear of the collar.
- 8.00-8.50 (12 f): R travels about 15 cm back. The heel is down by 8.30 and the pads are on the glaze by 8.50. Settled.

SH05, B4b (nominal 8.50-11.50):
- Settle to +5 f: the hand is still.
- 5 f after the settle (nominal 8.71), props fire the buzz, about 0.8 s long. PROP-02 lights face-down (edge glow, a secondary cue), rattles 3 mm at most and ticks against the mug, and fine rings run across the coffee (PROP-02 ST3).
- Nominal 9.50: the rattle stops, the phone settles back against the mug, the glow goes, and the rings flatten.
- The 7:05 card comes up as the rings flatten, within 9.25-9.75 s (script: 9.5 s).
- To 11.50: the hand holds and nothing moves. This tail absorbs any drift, so the cut stays at 11.5 s.

A drop anywhere in its window puts the card between 9.42 and 9.67 s. Take-selection priority: drop, landing, rings, still hand. The take starts on a holdable state (the hand still in its claw) and ends on one (the hand still on the mug, the coffee flat). Join fallback: at the settle (nominal 8.5 s), with 5 still frames after the join and none before. If blocker 2 forces the reframe, this join becomes the cut into the 30 cm SH05.
scenes.emotional_shift:
- Before (7.0-8.5): the hand hasn't stopped since 0.8 s. Every object it reaches, it takes, moves and leaves.
- Trigger (nominal 8.71 s): the phone rattles against the mug she is touching. The tick is audible, and rings run through the coffee under her fingers.
- After: the hand doesn't move, not toward the phone and not tighter. It is still on the mug at 11.5 s, after the phone has gone quiet and the coffee has flattened.
Visible change: for the first time in the spot, her hand stays on something instead of moving on, and it outlasts the phone. The dripper stands on the oak, out of the exchange, so no calm is credited to it.
scenes.transition_in: A hard cut at 7.0 s from SH03 on the same 55° axis, widening across the ellipsis. PROP-01 is still on PROP-03, now spent, with R already in its claw. The eye goes from the bloom to the dripper on the mug. Silence crosses the cut, and the plink (nominal 7.25 s) is the first new sound.
scenes.transition_out: At 11.5 s: a same-axis 1.7x cut-in on the time jump into SH06 at C5. The hand and mug vanishing carry the cut, and the size change marks it. Across the jump, the hand, the mug, its steam and the spent filter are gone. PROP-01 (reset exactly to 232.7/280) and the face-down PROP-02 keep their world positions. The eye goes from the still hand and the flat coffee to the dripper, right of centre beside the bare oak where the mug stood. The 7:05 card ends on the cut, and 'Hand-glazed stoneware.' comes on with the 'Solace' sign-off. Room tone crosses the cut, and the kettle's cooling tick starts after it. If SH05 was reframed, this becomes a hard cut on the time jump with the same carries: the dripper sits lower-right in SH05 and lands just right of centre in SH06.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'Before the phone, the inbox, or anyone else gets a piece of you, there are five minutes that are only yours — marked by the pour.' Carried by B4b (SH05): PROP-02's second buzz reaches her coffee through the mug it was flipped against, shows as rings under R, and gets nothing back. The 7:05 card names when it will get her. Cut this and the viewer loses the proof that the five minutes hold past the first refusal, and when they end. The flip becomes a one-off gesture.
practical_or_compositing_flags: SH04 last drip, which is the product's own output. Method: practical at 100% speed, relying on the drip timing (blocker 4). Acceptance: one drop leaves the exit hole into the coffee between 7.17 and 7.42 s. No drop lands on the outer glaze, the mug rim or the oak during the carry. Any later drop after the set-down falls inside the foot ring, out of sight, and props wipe it at the SH06 reset. Risk: a drip on the outside reads as a leaky dripper, and a missing drop loses the real detail.

SH04 set-down and release. Method: practical takes, each checked against the taped mark on the monitor. Acceptance: the foot lands within ±1 cm of 232.7/280, by hand and without looking, with the front at 235° and the foot clearing the rim before it descends. The release takes at least 5 f (6 planned) and doesn't nudge the dripper. The fingertips never touch the spent filter, and the oak shows no drip spot or mark. The take holds wherever the dripper lands, and props reset it exactly for SH06. Risk: a spot on the oak reads as a mark the product leaves.

SH05 coffee rings, which carry the turn with the sound off. Method: practical, only after blocker 2 passes at SH05's frame size. No composited rings. Acceptance, judged on the finished shot with the card laid in, on a 6-inch phone at 100%: TILE-01's reflected edge is seen to bend in the coffee during the rattle, and it is straight again as the card comes up. The rings start with the rattle, never before, and the card never covers the coffee. Her knuckles and fingertips don't move frame to frame, and the mug doesn't slide. If the bend doesn't read at 42 cm, SH05 is reframed at about 30 cm, with the settle join as plan of record (blocker 2). Risk: rings too small to read lose the sound-off turn, and rings that seem to come from her hand read as a tremor, turning the refusal into nerves.

SH05 hand still. Method: practical, with no generated plate. Acceptance: the heel stays on the oak at about 225.7/295. The pads stay over 225-315° below the rim, with the palm clear and the thumb along the index. The handle, the chip and the phone contact stay clear, and the hand stays at least 1 cm off the case in plan. No finger moves from the settle to 11.5 s. Risk: a fidget reads as anxiety and softens the refusal.

SH05 phone glow and rattle, a secondary cue. Method: the rattle is practical, from the real buzz. The glow is practical, and any composite matches a reference plate of the real phone face-down in its case under the SH05 light. Acceptance: the glow matches the reference in which edges leak, how far the light reaches (5-15 mm, ASSUMED) and how bright it is. Nothing is legible. The glow lasts only as long as the buzz. The rattle travels 3 mm at most, and the phone ends touching the mug. Risk: a glow brighter or wider than the reference tips into notification drama.

SH04-SH05 as one 4.5 s take, which chains a timed drip, a ±1 cm landing, a cued buzz, readable rings and a dead-still hand. Method: practical, locked, with the settle join as the fallback. Acceptance: no jump in the hand, the mug, the steam, the phone or the dripper. The rack, her torso and L never enter frame. The steam stays as thin threads, with none added. Risk: a visible join, or heavy steam that reads as stock lifestyle footage.

scenes.performance_beats:
The product's scene, with no person and no performance. Hero beat: the whole SH06 hold on PROP-01, with the thickest arc of its glaze pool facing the lens: the mark her thumb crossed in SH02A. Nothing in frame moves (script).

Real detail: the phone is still face-down exactly where she flipped it, and its mug-side edge now meets bare oak where the mug stood. She took the coffee and left the phone (world bible S4; ruling 7). If SH06's readability test shows only the case corner, the detail becomes the case corner beside bare oak. Mark 2 is texture only, and it is outside this frame.

Taste note 'The product is a tool, then a hero': the dripper worked in S1-S3 and closes the spot, with no logo card.

Entry: PROP-01 ST5 (reset exactly on 232.7/280, filter out, empty, outer glaze dry). PROP-02 ST4. PROP-03 gone. PROP-07 ST2. PROP-08 plugged in, off frame. No steam. PROP-06 cools off frame and is heard only.
Exit: unchanged.
scenes.blocking:
Nobody is in frame. PROP-01 stands at 232.7/280, inside the clear zone (x 221.7-243.7, y 269-291, 0-25 cm above the top), with its front at 235° facing the lens. PROP-02 lies face-down and dark at 230.0/302.8, 8 cm outside the clear zone. The mug's spot (232.7/295) is bare oak between them.

SH06: one locked frame at C5 on 55°, about 25 cm across at the dripper's plane (ruling 8). It replaces the earlier plan of a 34 cm B5 plus a B6 cut-in. The dripper sits 3-4 cm right of centre. On plan:
- the bare mug footprint is about 12 cm frame-left of the dripper;
- the case's mug-side edge enters about 13 cm frame-left of the dripper and runs out past the frame edge;
- the old contact point (232.7/299) is only about 1.5 cm inside the frame edge.
Script B5-B6 keep the phone at the frame edge, so at least 3 cm of the case stays in under both cards. PROP-04 is well frame-right, out of frame.
Cards and the sign-off sit in the world bible's bare card area on the wall-D paint (125 cm up and above), clear of the dripper and the case edge.

SH08 (D02-2): the same dripper mark on a separate 4:5 plate, with PROP-02 and PROP-08 struck and bare oak around it. It stays bare as the DTC plate (ruling 7).
scenes.action_progression:
SH06, B5-B6 (11.5-15.0): one locked hold of 84 f at 24 fps.
- 'Hand-glazed stoneware.' runs from 11.5 to 13.0 s.
- 'Shop the Solace dripper.' runs from 13.0 to 15.0 s.
- The 'Solace' sign-off runs from 11.5 to 15.0 s, across the card change.
Only the cards change; nothing in the picture moves. SH08 is the same state as a still.
scenes.emotional_shift: Hold. There is no trigger: nothing moves and nobody is there. The turn landed in the cut: the coffee went with her, and the phone stayed. The held frame lets it land.
scenes.transition_in: A same-axis 1.7x cut-in at 11.5 s from SH05 (see S3 transition_out). The eye lands on the dripper right of centre, with bare oak where the mug stood and the case edge at frame left.
scenes.transition_out: There is no internal cut: the card change at 13.0 s is the only change. The spot ends on a hard out on the held frame at 15.0 s, with no fade and no logo card (taste reject). Room tone and the kettle's tick run to the last frame. If the platform loops, the cut back to SH01's lit, face-up phone reads as the next 7:00.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'Before the phone, the inbox, or anyone else gets a piece of you, there are five minutes that are only yours — marked by the pour.' Carried by SH06: PROP-01 at rest beside the bare oak where the mug stood and the edge of the face-down PROP-02, so the spent marker of the pour sits next to the phone she refused. If the SH06 test shows only the case corner, the link is instead PROP-01 beside the face-down case corner and bare oak, and the cut test is unchanged. Cut this and the viewer loses the readable closing product moment (a must-include), the glaze pool that shows 'hand-glazed', the CTA and the last sight of the refused phone. They would know the ritual but not what to buy.
practical_or_compositing_flags: claim_demo_needs_clearance. SH06 and SH08 demonstrate the verified fact 'Hand-glazed stoneware' through the uneven glaze pool. Method: a practical packshot on the client's real unit, with no retouch that adds, moves or exaggerates the pooling. The world bible's glaze, colour and dimensions are ASSUMED, and no reference has been inspected. Acceptance: the pool on screen matches the physical unit side by side, and the clear zone is free of drops, grounds, fingerprints and crumbs. Risk: a generated or painted pool is fabricated proof of hand-glazing.

Readability of the closing product moment. Method: a real-unit test at C5, on the camera plan's frame and its tighter test variant, viewed on a 6-inch phone at 100% with both cards on. Acceptance: the pool's thickest 4 cm arc reads under both cards. The bare mug footprint and the case's mug-side edge read together as 'where the mug stood, next to the phone', with at least 3 cm of the case in. No card overlaps the dripper or the case edge. If the footprint and the edge don't read together, the ruled frame stays, and the link and the real detail switch to the case corner beside bare oak, as already written. Risk: the must-include fails, or the CTA plays over a packshot with no idea in it.

A locked 84-frame hold with nothing moving. Method: a practical plate, not a generated clip. Acceptance: no shimmer, drift or boiling on the product from 11.5 to 15.0 s, and the phone stays dark. Risk: drift reads as synthetic.

Reflections in the gloss pool and the rim band. Method: practical; how they are controlled is the Cinematographer's call. Must show: only the bare flats, CEIL-01 and TILE-01's edge (the world bible's mirror paths), plus at most an unreadable dark shape. Must not show: crew, rig or a light. No retouch on the pool. Risk: a reflected rig in the DTC image can't be painted out without touching the claim.

Wetness only grows. Method: practical. For SH06 the cone interior keeps the faint damp sheen it had after the brew, and the outer glaze is checked dry before each take. SH08 is a separate plate and can be fully dry. Acceptance: no drops, grounds or fibres, and dry outer glaze. Risk: a bone-dry interior breaks continuity, and drops on the outside read as a leak.

Supers. Method: composite (the editor's). Acceptance: no card or sign-off ever overlaps the dripper or covers the case edge at frame left. Risk: text over the product costs the readable closing moment, and text over the phone costs the idea.

assumptions: Timings follow the revised script: B1 0-1.5, B2 1.5-4.5, B3 4.5-7.0, B4a 7.0-8.5, B4b 8.5-11.5, B5 11.5-13.0, B6 13.0-15.0, with the 7:05 card at 9.5 s. I retimed the review's figures to match: the S3-to-S4 cut-in moves from 11.0 to 11.5 s, SH06 goes from 96 f to 84 f, and the join moves from 9.0 to 8.5 s. The decisions themselves are unchanged.

Package-review rulings recorded here. (1) The rack is out of SH01, which is about 34 cm across. (2) SH02A/SH02B are approved. The filter-collar fix at x≈241 is moot, because the revised script puts the filter in during the B2/B3 cut. (3) SH03 keeps the phone's dark end in frame, the paint-out fallback is withdrawn, and the S2 break is declared. (4) SH04-SH05 is one take; reopened only if the ring test fails at SH05's frame size. (5) The SH05 wrist crossing the port end is accepted. (6) SH02A's 18 f are accepted. (7) S4's real detail is the phone left where she flipped it, Mark 2 is texture, and SH08 stays bare. (8) SH06 is one locked hold of about 25 cm at C5. (9) The SH01 grip is confirmed as written. (10) The SH02A fallback is a pickup, not generation. (11) The wall-B camera-plan blocker is deleted.

This round's changes. (1) B3's objective is now 'start the bloom from the centre out without the stream touching the paper', with one pass mark and a stated minimum. (2) B4a is rebalanced to 4/4/10/6/12 f: the release gets 6 f and the travel-and-settle 12 f. The drop ends the hold, the buzz is cued off the settle, and the card follows the rings within ±0.25 s of 9.5 s. (3) The SH02A card comes in at 1.5 s with a world position and a phone-size thumb test, with a 25 cm fallback. (4) SH05 gets a phone-size ring test, with a 30 cm reframe on 31-55° as the fallback. (5) SH06 gets a footprint-and-edge test, with a conditional link. (6) Other departments' method and the lens figures are removed.

The latest note removes lens and distance figures, while an earlier note asked for the S2 break to cite '100mm at 1.0 m'. I give the reason as SH03's frame width, about 20 cm, which is the substance of that reason. Lens and distance stay with the camera plan.

Treatment blockers closed as superseded: the wall-B camera plan; the SH01-SH02 pace problem (solved by SH02A/SH02B); the '7:00' read (solved by taking the rack out of SH01); and the B6 phone-edge plan of record (replaced by the single C5 hold).

Shot IDs: SH01 = B1. SH02A/SH02B = B2 (18 + 54 f, seat on SH02B f15). SH03 = B3. SH04 = B4a. SH05 = B4b (a 30 cm variant only if blocker 2 fails). SH06 = B5-B6 (84 f at C5). SH07 = D02-1. SH08 = D02-2.

No tool binding was given, so every uncut action is 5 s or less. Every hand and product plate is still practical, and every fallback is a pickup. The longest uncut take is SH04-SH05 at 4.5 s. The composites are the '7:00' lock screen, any match on the SH05 glow, and the supers.

Hands: NORA is right-handed. R does SH01, SH02A, SH02B, SH04 and SH05. L pours in SH03 (seen only as the spout) and SH07, where its fingers are the one exception to 'L never in frame'. Both of R's product grips cross the rim, so casting's breadth check applies to the rim diameter.

The prop marks are the world bible's final set. NORA's marks are mine: N2 is centred at y 308, facing 90°, and the rack mark is at y 215. The body figures (167 cm, right shoulder about 137 cm up) are ASSUMED. Lateral and depth figures are plan figures at counter height. The frame widths are targets, and lens, height and lighting are the Cinematographer's.

Deliberate taste-note break: 'One real detail per scene' in S2. SH03 carries the pour alone, and the scorch band moves to SH07. Cutting the window shot is the script's own break from the route, and I follow it. No other taste note is broken.

Hypotheses, not verified: (1) about 6-7 g of water (about 4 g/s for 1.6 s) visibly starts a bloom on 18-20 g of grounds at 100% speed; (2) the phone's buzz ripples the coffee through the phone-to-mug contact, with her hand resting on the mug; (3) a cone drained until drips slow to about one a second will have a drop hanging at 7.0 s. None of these is a product claim.

Changes across the time cuts are ellipses, never off-screen hand-offs. S1 to S2: the filter and grounds go in, and L takes the kettle. S2 to S3: the kettle goes back and the coffee draws down. S3 to S4: the mug is taken, the filter binned, the steam gone, and the dripper reset.

The fictional NORA is played by a hand double matched to the casting anchors. No real person's name, likeness or identity is used. The D02 stills are separate 4:5 plates, not crops of the native 9:16 D01.

No reference was inspected, because no reference_reader is bound. The product's look, size and glaze are ASSUMED in the world bible. The camera plan itself was not supplied, so I cite only the IDs and figures the review notes give from it: C5, SH02A/SH02B, the 1.7x cut-in, and the frame sizes.

blockers.issue: The camera plan was drawn on the previous script's times: SH03 to 7.5 s, SH04-SH05 from 7.5 to 11.0 s, and SH06 as 96 f from 11.0 s. The revised script moves B3 to 4.5-7.0 and B4a/B4b to 7.0-8.5/8.5-11.5, puts B5-B6 at 11.5-15.0, and adds B2's thumb pass, which moves NORA's rack mark from y 248 to y 215. SH02A was cleared against the old mark.
blockers.resolution: If the plan hasn't been retimed yet, re-issue it with the following. SH03 at 4.5-7.0 (60 f). SH04-SH05 at 7.0-11.5 (108 f) as one take, joined if needed at the settle (nominal 8.5 s), with the buzz cued off the settle. SH06 at C5 as one locked 84 f hold from 11.5 s, cut in 1.7x from SH05. SH02A (18 f, 25°) and SH02B (54 f, 55°, seat on f15) keep their lengths. Re-check SH02A with NORA at y 215 (chest at y 196-234, x ≤195), and hold a tighter 25 cm variant for the thumb test. Hold a 30 cm SH05 variant on a bearing between 31° and 55° in case blocker 2 fails.

blockers.issue: The sound-off read of the B4b turn rests on the buzz rippling the coffee through the phone-to-mug contact. This is untested. Her fingertips on the mug and her heel on the oak may damp the vibration, and even real rings may be too small to read: in the 42 cm frame the coffee is about 1.2 cm wide on a 6-inch phone.
blockers.resolution: Run a pre-shoot test at SH05's frame (about 42 cm on 55°) at 100% speed. Set-up: the hand double's R in the B4b position (heel at about 225.7/295; pads over 225-315° below the rim, palm clear, thumb along the index); fresh hot coffee at the tide line with thin steam; the real phone in the PROP-02 case touching the mug on the PROP-07 oak; one buzz of about 0.8 s, fired on cue within 2 f. Pass: judged on a 6-inch phone at 100%, with the 7:05 card laid in, TILE-01's reflected edge is seen to bend in the coffee during the rattle. If it bends but doesn't read, re-test at about 30 cm on a bearing between 31° and 55°. If that passes, the settle join becomes plan of record, with SH05 reframed (ruling 4 reopened). If no rings form at any size, fit a concealed coin vibration motor inside the case's back plate, fire it on the buzz cue, and re-run both steps with the hand in place. If everything fails, SH05 is held as written and the turn rests on the still hand and the 7:05 card, with no composited rings. Tell the Copywriter and me before the shoot.

blockers.issue: The B3 pass mark (the whole bed darkened and the centre visibly risen, by at least about 5 mm, by 6.7 s) is a hypothesis: about 6-7 g of water lands on 18-20 g of grounds in a 1.6 s pour. PROP-05 ST4's 'domed about 1 cm' becomes the target, not the pass.
blockers.resolution: Run a pre-shoot bloom test on the real unit, at SH03's frame on 55°, at 100% speed. Coffee: roasted 5-14 days before the shoot and ground on the day, medium-fine, 18-20 g, heaped as in PROP-05 ST3. Water just off the boil, from PROP-06. Pour rate: about 4 g/s through the 5 mm spout, as two circuits in 1.6 s. Pass: the pass mark, read on a 6-inch phone at 100%. If it fails, B3 is staged as written, and the smallest fix goes to the Copywriter: change B3's picture from 'swell, bubble and dome up against the paper' to 'darken and start to rise', with no timing change.

blockers.issue: B4a needs a drop hanging at the exit hole when the take rolls, but PROP-01 ST4 says props drain the cone first 'so nothing else drips'. How a drop is there at 7.0 s is a hypothesis.
blockers.resolution: Amend PROP-01 ST4 so that props let the cone drain until drips slow to about one a second, and roll so the lift comes about 0.5-0.8 s after the last drip. Test at the prelight on the real unit. Pass: a drop falls into the coffee within 7.17-7.42 s in at least one take in three, and no second drop falls during the 0.42 s carry. If it fails, the smallest fix is the script's own B4a: the drop falls during the 3 cm lift, the hold goes, and its 4 f go to the release. The real detail stays: she doesn't carry the cone until the drop has fallen.

blockers.issue: The script runs 'Nobody gets you before the pour.' across both B2 angles, so it comes in at 1.5 s on the same cut as the SH02A thumb pass (1.50-1.75 s), which sets up 'Hand-glazed stoneware.' A card coming up pulls the eye. This is pending the SH02A phone test.
blockers.resolution: Staged as written. If the phone test shows the card pulling the eye off the thumb, the smallest fix is for the card to come in on the SH02B cut at 2.25 s and hold to 4.5 s (2.25 s on screen). The Copywriter approves or refuses before the edit.
