evidence.specificity: All six previous notes were addressed, and each fix added something a crew can act on. Blocking is given as world coordinates tied to the world bible's marks: "B4b: R comes about 15 cm back toward wall C, opposite the way it went out, and settles. The heel sits on the oak at about 225.7/295, 3 cm in front of the mug and at least 2 cm clear of the case (y ≥299)." The ring test now works at display size: "Acceptance, judged on the finished shot with the card laid in, on a 6-inch phone at 100%: TILE-01's reflected edge is seen to bend in the coffee during the rattle, and it is straight again as the card comes up." The bloom has one pass mark: "by 6.7 s the whole visible bed has darkened, and the centre has risen enough to see on a 6-inch phone at 100%. The minimum is about 5 mm, and about 1 cm is the target, not the pass." The SH02A card has a world position and a phone-size thumb test with a 25 cm fallback. The only follow-up a board artist would need is small: SH02B has no frame-width target, and SH01 has no sub-step for the hand's entry (see notes).
evidence.distinctiveness: The beats could only belong to this idea and this set. "Real detail: she flips it while it is still plugged in. It charged here overnight (PROP-08), and she doesn't unplug it to refuse it." "Real detail: she waits out the last drip over the mug instead of carrying a dripping cone." "Scene detail: the rings bending TILE-01's reflected edge (script, world bible)." S4 ends on "the phone is still face-down exactly where she flipped it, and its mug-side edge now meets bare oak where the mug stood." Swap in a competitor's dripper and the glaze-pool thumb pass and its SH06 payoff break.
evidence.fit: R1 is sharper here than as written, and every link quotes the route line verbatim and passes the cut test: "Cut this and the viewer loses the proof that the five minutes hold past the first refusal, and when they end. The flip becomes a one-off gesture." No unverified benefit is credited to the product: "The dripper plays no part in the trigger, so nothing credits it with calming her," and in S3, "The dripper stands on the oak, out of the exchange, so no calm is credited to it." The verified fact is shown practically and flagged: "claim_demo_needs_clearance. SH06 and SH08 demonstrate the verified fact 'Hand-glazed stoneware' through the uneven glaze pool. Method: a practical packshot on the client's real unit, with no retouch that adds, moves or exaggerates the pooling." Both must-includes are met: the product has a clear role as the tool, and the closing product moment gets a readability test. There is no luxury imagery, no window shot and no slow motion ("Everything plays at 100% speed").
evidence.craft: The previous craft notes are fixed. (1) B4a is rebalanced and adds up: "7.75-8.00 (6 f): release. The fingertips open off the outer glaze, and R rises 2 cm clear of the collar." 4+4+10+6+12 = 36 f. (2) The drop has a tested mechanism (blocker 4), the timing is cued rather than clocked, and the slack is absorbed: "A drop anywhere in its window puts the card between 9.42 and 9.67 s. Take-selection priority: drop, landing, rings, still hand." (3) The B3 objective can now be performed ("start the bloom from the centre out without the stream touching the paper"), and blocker 3 names freshness, grind and pour rate. (4) SH05 and SH02A have phone-size tests with fallbacks. (5) SH06 has a conditional link. (6) Other departments' method is mostly out ("how they are controlled is the Cinematographer's call"; "Method: composite (the editor's)"). The prop state IDs, marks, screen direction ("R exits SH01 frame right and enters SH02A from frame left") and sub-step sums all check out on plan. Three things hold it at 8. First, a silent rewrite of approved sound: "props fire the buzz, about 0.8 s long" against the script's "One phone buzz, about 1.0s long". Second, the left-hand pour risk is wider than it needs to be and has no fallback. Third, the scene text still leans on review rulings ("(ruling 9)", "(ruling 4 reopened)") instead of the decisions themselves.

looks.garment_silhouette: Closet: mid-price, bought once and kept. She spends on her work coat, boots and paper, and skimps on house clothes (retired knits, old sleepwear). At 7:00 she isn't dressed for anyone yet: she's in house clothes, with the work coat and boots still by the door (backstory only, nothing added to the set). The look says the day hasn't claimed her yet (Route R1). Story: a weekday at 7:00, early November 2026, USA (ASSUMED). It is about 6 °C outside and 19 °C in the kitchen while the radiator warms (ASSUMED). So she wears wool over a tee, trousers to the floor and socks: ankles covered, shoes by the door. Head to toe: (1) crewneck pullover, hem at the hip bone, sleeve ending in the lower third of the forearm, 7 cm above the wrist bone at rest and 9 cm when reaching or pouring; (2) short-sleeve crew tee under it, hem 3 cm below the pullover hem; (3) elastic-waist sleep trousers, full length, hem on the top of the foot; (4) crew socks to mid-calf; (5) no footwear. Older than the story: the pullover, bought around 2020. Two winters ago a 60 °C wash felted it and shrank the sleeves off her wrists. That made it her kitchen sweater, with nothing to push up before the pour. It is wardrobe's one real detail (taste notes: 'One real detail per scene') and the only garment the viewer sees (taste notes: 'Hands before faces'). Duplicates: use untreated, non-superwash 100% merino, because superwash won't felt. Start from a 12-gauge single-jersey crew one size up. Give it one 60 °C wash and one tumble dry, and a second dry only if it is still short of the numbers. Test one sample first, because shrink varies by yarn. Make 3, since a splash during the pour means a swap. Finished sizes, measured flat (ASSUMED from the 167 cm casting spec): sleeve 52 cm from shoulder seam to cuff edge; body 58 cm from neck-shoulder point to hem; chest 96 cm; cuff circumference 20 cm (forearm girth 7 cm above the wrist bone is about 19 cm, plus 1 cm ease). The fitting resets these on the hand double so the cuff lands 7 cm above the wrist bone with the hand flat on the counter. Every duplicate then matches the hero within ±0.5 cm. Pills: rub each inner forearm, 5-10 cm above the cuff, on the eased edge of an UNTINTED cured oiled-oak offcut until it matches the hero. Untinted, so the new tobacco tint on the PROP-07 finish can't transfer to the wool.
looks.materials_colors:
Pullover: untreated (non-superwash) 100% merino single jersey, 12-gauge, felted to about 330 g/m² (ASSUMED), ink blue #1F2A40. Matte and fuzzed flat, so no stitch reads. Cuff: a 4 cm band knitted 1x1 rib and felted solid in the same #1F2A40, with no wales visible. Small pills on both inner forearms, where she rests them on the counter's worn front edge (PROP-07 Mark 2). It holds its shape and doesn't slide. Risk: it sheds fibres, so lint-roll between setups; a blue fibre on the glaze or the oak means a reshoot. Tee (unseen): cotton single jersey 160 g/m², brown-black #2C2826. Trousers (unseen): brushed cotton flannel 170 g/m², slate grey #5A5E66. Socks (unseen): merino-nylon plain knit, charcoal #3A3A3D. Hair elastic (unseen): matte fabric-covered, black #2A2728 approx. Everything is plain unmarked fabric: no logo, label, stripe or print.
Approx LCh (sRGB, D65, hand-computed, all approx). Product (PROP-01): body #E3D9C6 L* 87, C* 11, h 88°; glaze pool #B59A72 L* 65, C* 25, h 80°; rim band #C9A77E L* 71, C* 27, h 76°; raw foot #A88663 L* 58, C* 25, h 71°. Product hues span 71-88°.
Pullover #1F2A40: L* 17, C* 16, h 279°, at least 152° from every product hue. Clears on hue.
Tee #2C2826: L* 16, C* 2, h 55°. It is 34° from the body (within 5° of the line), 25° from the pool, 21° from the rim and 16° from the foot. It clears on C* 2 and on L* (42+ below every surface). Nearest alternative that clears on hue: cool charcoal #2B2C30 (L* 18, C* 3, h 282°).
Trousers #5A5E66 (L* 40, C* 5, h 273°), socks #3A3A3D (L* 25, C* 2, h 291°) and elastic #2A2728 (L* 16, C* 2, h 354°) all clear on hue by 77° or more.
Built skin marks. These are casting anchors, not worn colour, and are never shifted to clear the product. Mole #3B2519 approx, right hand: L* 17, C* 15, h 55°. It clears on L*, 41+ below every product surface. Scar #8A6650 approx, left hand: L* 46, C* 21, h 58°. It is 13° from the foot, 18° from the rim, 22° from the pool and 30° from the body. As a worn colour it would fail against the foot, rim and pool (C* 21, only 12-25 L* apart). It stays because it is 10 × 1.5 mm, it sits on the hand that closes on the kettle handle in D02-1 rather than on the dripper, and styling never alters skin for separation.
Value: the sleeve (L* 17) is 18 below the skin #6F4A34 (L* 35, C* 23, h 56°) and 70 below the dripper body, which meets casting's value rule. It is 10 below the tinted oak #533C2B (L* 27, C* 16, h 62°) and 143° from it in hue, and 32 below the phone case #77756F (L* 49): blue against warm brown and neutral grey. The skin sits only about 8 L* above the new oak, so the sleeve gives the forearm its edge. The hand's own edge on the oak, and against the raw foot in the grip (23 L*), is the camera plan's job. Widest-frame read: warm brown hand plus ink-blue sleeve, the only blue on the set, inside the world bible's 8% out-of-palette share.
looks.fit_notes: Fitted on the hand double's arms. Pullover: shoulder seam 1 cm inside the shoulder point (shrunk), 6 cm chest ease, hem at the hip bone. The sleeve is close through the forearm, and the cuff band has 1 cm ease, so it grips and can't slide down. The sleeve ends in the lower third of the forearm. At rest (hand flat, or heel of the hand on the oak as in D01-B4b) it sits 7 cm above the wrist bone. Reaching or pouring it sits 9 cm (±1) above: reaching means to the rack, the B2 lift or the B4a lift; pouring means the left arm raised with the kettle tipped, as in D02-1 (director's left-hand restage). It is never under 5 cm above the wrist bone on either arm (casting minimum), and both arms match. No fabric crosses the dripper, filter, kettle, stream, mug or phone in any reach. Tee: sleeve hem hidden at mid-bicep, body hem 3 cm below the pullover. Trousers: mid rise, 8 cm hip ease, full break, back hem 1 cm off the floor. Socks: tops at mid-calf, under the trousers. Closures: 0 on every garment; keep it at 0. In frame: only the cuffs and 5-15 cm of sleeve, in D01-B1, B2, B4a, B4b and D02-1. D01-B3 shows only the spout, so no wardrobe is in that frame.
accessories: None on the hands or wrists: no ring, watch, bracelet, hair elastic, plaster, tape or finger cot. Per casting, a ring would click on stoneware over the designed sound, including the phone's tick against the mug at B4b, and a watch is a second clock against 7:00 and 7:05.
No apron and no towel over the shoulder, because either would drift into frame over the counter.
One matte black fabric-covered elastic, #2A2728 approx, in the hair only and never on the wrist.
No earrings, necklace or glasses: head and neck are never in frame.
looks.hair_makeup:
Skin, in casting's words. Back of hand and forearm: medium-deep, warm undertone, #6F4A34 approx. Palms and fingertip pads: medium, warm undertone, #B3886A approx. Knuckle creases: deep, warm undertone, #4A2F20 approx. Words and hexes go in the hand-double call and the acceptance checks. Prompts carry the words only (broad square hand, medium-deep skin, warm undertone, creased knuckles, short bare nails), because generators lighten, lengthen and smooth hands. Creases, veins and forearm hair are cast for, not built. The forearm hair #2A1E17 approx, sparse and fine along the outer edge of both forearms, stays as it is (the stylist's call, per casting), with no shaving on the day. No body makeup and no powder (it greys brown skin); pores stay visible. Finish matte: no hand cream or oil on the day; blot any sheen with a tissue. The only concealing: any mark of the double's own on either hand or forearm (mole, scar, tattoo) is covered with alcohol-activated paint matched to #6F4A34 and sealed matte, so the two built marks are the only marks.
Nails (joint lock with casting): no manicure, cuticle push-back or cuticle oil for 7 days before the shoot. On the day: free edge 1 mm or less, filed straight across, unpolished and unbuffed. The right thumb cuticle is left untrimmed so it reads slightly ragged.
MOLE, right hand only. Flat, round, 4 mm (±0.3), #3B2519 approx, matte, with a 0.3 mm soft edge and no relief. With the hand flat, it sits on the back of the right hand, on the line of the middle-finger bone, centred 2 cm toward the wrist from the middle-finger knuckle. At the fitting, cut a clear acetate template to the double's right hand, mark the knuckles and wrist bone on it, and punch a 4 mm hole at that point. Primary method: a printed skin-safe transfer, 10 printed from one file, with the print proofed against a #3B2519 swatch card in daylight. Backup: alcohol-activated paint stippled through the hole. Clean the skin with an alcohol wipe, let it dry, apply, then seal matte.
SCAR, left hand only (new from casting). A pale, flat, matte line, 10 mm (±1) long and 1.5 mm wide, with tapered ends and no relief, #8A6650 approx (lighter than the skin around it). It runs across the back of the left index finger, side to side, centred on the crest of the middle joint with the finger straight. Method: alcohol-activated paint mixed to a #8A6650 swatch card (a transfer would crack over a flexing joint). Apply it through a 10 × 1.5 mm slot in a left-hand acetate template marked at the index knuckle and middle joint, then seal with a flexible matte sealer. The joint's creases still read through as texture; only the tone lifts. Then close the hand fully on a dowel the size of the kettle handle 5 times. If the scar cracks, smears or shines, redo it before camera.
Patch-test every product on the double 48 h before the shoot. Photograph the fitting application on both hands beside a ruler; that photo is the reference.
CHECK AND REAPPLY at the start of each hand setup (D01-B1, B2, B4a, B4b, D02-1), and again after any hand wash or contact with water, coffee or steam:
(1) Right hand flat, template on. The mole sits in the hole within ±1 mm, measures 4 mm, matches its card, is matte and has an unbroken edge.
(2) Left hand flat, template on. The scar sits in the slot within ±1 mm, matches its card, and has no crack or shine.
(3) No other mark on either hand or forearm.
(4) Photograph both hands beside the ruler and log the time and the mole unit number.
Fixes: shine gets re-sealed. Anything else (a smudge, drift over 1 mm, a crack, a lift, colour off the card) means remove it, reapply and re-run the check. On the first take of each setup, confirm on the monitor that the mole is on the right hand and the scar is on the left.
Generation: every generated frame showing the back of the right hand is checked against CHR-NORA-HAND@v1 for the mole. Every generated frame showing the back of the left hand is checked against CHR-NORA-HAND@v1 for the scar. No hex codes go in prompts: identity lives in the reference and the acceptance check.
Hair (ASSUMED, never in frame): black-brown #2A1E17 approx to match the forearm hair; wavy (2B), to mid shoulder blade, centre part. Twist it into a low knot at the nape with the one elastic, so no strand falls forward over the pour. Face: not cast, no makeup, never in frame (taste notes: 'Hands before faces'). She reads by two colour blocks (brown hand, ink-blue sleeve) plus casting's broad, square hand shape.

assumptions: Season and temperature are ASSUMED: early November 2026, about 6 °C outside and 19 °C inside, in the world bible's assumed USA 2026 setting. The brief gives no season.

The hue check uses the world bible's PROP-01 hexes (body #E3D9C6, pool #B59A72, rim #C9A77E, raw foot #A88663). These are ASSUMED, because the client gave no product colour. If the real glaze differs, rerun the check.

All L*, C* and h values are hand-computed from hex (sRGB, D65) and approximate. New in this version: the counter's tinted oak #533C2B (L* 27, C* 16, h 62°) replaces #7A5A3E; the phone case #77756F (L* 49) replaces #3E4447; and the left-hand scar #8A6650 (L* 46, C* 21, h 58°) is added.

I dropped the built callus. Casting now makes it 'backstory, not a lock', and no longer gives a size, hex or placement for it. A built mark that nobody checks drifts between setups and generations, so it is not built. Dropping it also removes the one skin tone that sat 11° from the raw foot at C* 22 inside the dripper grip. The review note's wording named 'the mole and callus', so the Generation line now names the mole on the right hand and the new scar on the left. Everything else is as the note asked: acceptance against CHR-NORA-HAND@v1, and no hex codes in prompts.
I have not seen CHR-NORA-HAND@v1. It must show the mole on the right hand, the scar on the left, and no callus. If it doesn't, generation should reissue it before any hand frame is accepted.

Casting's skin anchor says the words go 'with the hex codes' into every prompt. I follow the generation plan's rule, as the review note cites it: the words go in prompts, and the hexes go only in the hand-double call and the acceptance checks. Casting's line should be aligned to match.

The left-hand scar is new from casting's anchors. Its length, colour, position and flatness are casting's. Its 1.5 mm width, tapered ends, side-to-side orientation and paint-not-transfer method are my ASSUMED build choices, for casting to sign off at the fitting.

The director's restage makes the pour left-handed, so the left hand is on the kettle in D02-1. The shot list isn't in my context, so I don't know which hand appears in D01-B1, B2, B4a and B4b. The mark locks are therefore written per hand, not per beat.
D01-B3 now shows only the spout, so the check-and-reapply setups drop B3 (it was listed in the last version).
The mole transfer runs to 10 units from one file. That count, the 48 h patch test and the 7-day no-manicure window are my working assumptions.
Knuckle creases, veins and forearm hair are matched at casting, not built or painted. If a double doesn't match, casting recasts. Casting left the forearm hair to the stylist, and it stays as it is.
Hair colour, curl (2B), length and part are ASSUMED and never in frame. They are specified only so no strand enters a frame and the knot can be rebuilt.
I kept the brown-black tee #2C2826 rather than the named alternative, #2B2C30. It is never in frame and it clears on C* 2. Swap it if any frame ever shows the neckline.

Finished sizes (sleeve 52, body 58, chest 96, cuff 20 cm) and the felted weight (about 330 g/m²) are ASSUMED from the 167 cm casting spec. The fitting resets them on the hand double, and duplicates then match the hero within ±0.5 cm.

evidence.specificity: Every layer is given with a landmark, a fibre, a weight and a hex, and the look could be rebuilt from the rail: "Pullover: untreated (non-superwash) 100% merino single jersey, 12-gauge, felted to about 330 g/m² (ASSUMED), ink blue #1F2A40" and "sleeve 52 cm from shoulder seam to cuff edge; body 58 cm from neck-shoulder point to hem; chest 96 cm; cuff circumference 20 cm". The built marks come with a method, a template and a tolerance: "MOLE, right hand only. Flat, round, 4 mm (±0.3), #3B2519 approx ... centred 2 cm toward the wrist from the middle-finger knuckle." The LCh check gives numbers for every worn colour and names the nearest alternative at the threshold: "Tee #2C2826: L* 16, C* 2, h 55°. It is 34° from the body (within 5° of the line) ... Nearest alternative that clears on hue: cool charcoal #2B2C30." Two gaps keep it from a 10. The sleeve locks are in centimetres, which nobody can measure in a frame without a scale. The page gives prompt words for the skin but none for the garment, and names no wardrobe reference for generation.
evidence.distinctiveness: The one real detail comes from the product's needs and the route, not from a mood board: "Two winters ago a 60 °C wash felted it and shrank the sleeves off her wrists. That made it her kitchen sweater, with nothing to push up before the pour." The accessory logic uses the script's own clocks: "a watch is a second clock against 7:00 and 7:05". The wear is tied to the set's Mark 2: "Small pills on both inner forearms, where she rests them on the counter's worn front edge (PROP-07 Mark 2)." Three things hold it at 8. On screen the viewer sees only a short, dark blue sleeve, and the pills sit on the underside of the forearm, facing the counter. #1F2A40 sits a few L* from the craft brief's calibration navy #26314A. And the look would carry to another pour-over brand unchanged.
evidence.fit: Lucas's R1 idea shows up in the clothes, sharper than he wrote it: "At 7:00 she isn't dressed for anyone yet: she's in house clothes, with the work coat and boots still by the door (backstory only, nothing added to the set). The look says the day hasn't claimed her yet (Route R1)." The page avoids the must-avoid on generic luxury by rejecting the category's stock hand: "None on the hands or wrists: no ring, watch, bracelet, hair elastic, plaster, tape or finger cot." It keeps the product role clear: "No fabric crosses the dripper, filter, kettle, stream, mug or phone in any reach." It makes no product claims. 'Hands before faces' and 'One real detail per scene' are cited where they apply. The ink blue sits outside the route's stoneware palette on purpose, inside the world bible's 8% out-of-palette share, and the page says so.
evidence.craft: This is senior makeup and wardrobe technique. The felting risk is caught ("use untreated, non-superwash 100% merino, because superwash won't felt"). The paint is chosen for a flexing joint ("alcohol-activated paint ... (a transfer would crack over a flexing joint)"). The scar is stress-tested before camera: "Then close the hand fully on a dowel the size of the kettle handle 5 times. If the scar cracks, smears or shines, redo it before camera." The note on brown skin is right: "No body makeup and no powder (it greys brown skin); pores stay visible." I recomputed the LCh values and they hold: pullover about L* 16, C* 17, h 285°; skin L* 35. Four things keep it at 8. The mirror-reject locks ("A mole on the left hand means the frame is mirrored: reject") contradict the world bible's flop fallback, and the page never addresses the craft rule against resting identity on asymmetric details. The hand double's consent is not named, and "The cast is fictional, and no real person's likeness or name is used" skips over a real person's hands being painted, patch-tested and photographed as the reference. A 20 cm felted cuff has no pass-over test on an 8.5 cm-broad hand. And three duplicates to ±0.5 cm by washing alone is optimistic.

cues.description: Room tone for NORA's kitchen: a small city flat at 7 a.m., heard close. What you hear: a fridge compressor's low, steady hum off screen (placed to match the world bible layout), and a thin wash of street traffic through a closed window, far off, with no horns or sirens. What's left out: birdsong (the dawn cliché); neighbours, TV or radio (nothing else in the room asks anything of her, so there's no background speech to clear); a clock tick (the phone's 7:00 is the only clock). It runs at one level, unbroken across every cut, and never drops to digital silence. The script's 'silence' is this tone on its own: B1 0.79-1.25 s (f19-f30, from the buzz cut to the pad knock); B1 1.25-1.50 s, running into B2 to 1.88 s (f30-f45, from the pad knock to the rack knock); B4b 10.00-11.50 s, running into B5 to 11.79 s (f240-f283, from the buzz stop to the first kettle tick). It also fills every other gap between the hits in 002-007. The longest are 3.00-4.70 s (f72-f113, from the seat-click ring-out to the kettle tip, under the B2 card and across the B2/B3 cut) and 8.46-9.21 s (f203-f221, from the set-down to the B4b buzz). Arc: the loudest moment is the B4b buzz, 9.21-10.00 s (f221-f240), where the face-down phone chatters on its four corner pads on the oak and ticks against the mug (006). The quietest is the tone alone straight after it (f240-f283), where the refusal lands. Muted viewers miss nothing: the 7:00 screen, the coffee rings, the glow and the cards carry the story. Feeds loop, so the level at 15.00 s matches 0.00 s and runs cleanly into the B1 buzz. Every D01 shot is a practical plate. Its production sound is a guide track only, nothing from it is cut in, and every cue is rebuilt from the foley session.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Preferred source: a wild room-tone track recorded for this production at the foley session, in a real apartment kitchen. This needs (1) a location release from the flat's occupant that covers sound recording, and (2) a written assignment of the recording and all rights in it from the recordist, covering all media, worldwide, in perpetuity, including use beyond D01 (the DTC product page and later cuts). Both pending. Fallback: a library ambience whose licence names advertising use ('royalty-free' is not a scope). The assumed scope, to be confirmed, is paid and organic social plus the Solace DTC site, one territory named by the producer, 12 months from first use. Pending. The practical plates' guide track is not used, so this cue needs no clearance for it. No clearly heard speech is planned. Any that gets recorded is removed or made unintelligible, so no speaker consent is needed. Owner for all of the above: producer.

cues.timing: D01-B1, 0.00-1.50 s: room tone 0.00-0.08 s (f0-f2); one buzz pulse 0.08-0.79 s (f2-f19, picture-led, ±2); room tone 0.79-1.25 s (f19-f30); pad knock 1.25 s (f30, picture-led, ±2); room tone 1.25-1.50 s (f30-f36), running into B2 to 1.88 s (f45)
cues.description: The hook. The first sync sound lands at 0.08 s, inside the 1.5 s rule. PROP-02 lies face-up with its flat case back flush on the PROP-07 oak (there's no raised camera module to rock on). One vibration pulse, picture-led to the 7:00 lock screen lighting up: a dense, even buzz chattering through the oak with no rocking tick, lighter and brighter than B4b. Vibration only, no OS alert tone. The pulse ends at f19, the frame NORA's hand lands on the phone, so her hand reads as cutting it off. In B4b the same pulse plays out whole. The grab, the flip and the hand's move right toward the rack get no foley ('Restraint over explanation'). Room tone alone runs to f30. At 1.25 s (f30) the phone lands face-down on its four corner pads, which stand 1.5 mm proud of the glass: one soft, low knock of the pads on wood, with no bounce and no glass sound, because the glass never touches. A corner pad settles against the empty chipped mug with no ceramic ring. Then room tone alone.

Never library glass or a library phone. The session records: face-up (back flush on the oak); face-down (on the pads, one corner pad against the mug); one pulse of at least 20 frames (B1 cuts it at the hand, B4b plays it whole); the pad knock; and one double-pulse take as a safety only. No platform or OS alert sounds. Needs a written assignment of the recordings and all rights in them from the foley artist and the recordist, covering all media, worldwide, in perpetuity, including use beyond D01 (the DTC product page and later cuts). Status: session and assignment pending. Owner: producer.

cues.timing: D01-B2, 1.50-4.50 s: room tone 1.50-1.88 s (f36-f45); rack knock 1.88-2.00 s (f45-f48); room tone through the carry and the cut 2.00-2.79 s (f48-f67); seat click 2.79 s (f67), ring gone by 3.00 s (f72); room tone 3.00-4.50 s (f72-f108), running into B3 to 4.70 s (f113). cues.description: 1.88-2.00 s (f45-f48): as the Solace dripper lifts off the dish rack, its stoneware foot knocks one coated-wire tine and slides clear. Light, dry, one contact. The thumb passing over the glaze and the low carry get no foley. The thumb doesn't stop, so the sound doesn't point at it either. 2.79 s (f67): the dripper seats on the chipped white mug's rim with a short, dense click of stoneware on ceramic and a brief low ring, gone by f72. Not a thin porcelain ping, not a plastic clack. The phone's corner pad against the mug gives nothing back. The hand lets go with no foley, and B2 ends on the empty dripper in room tone. Filter: the script puts the filter and grounds in during the B2/B3 cut, so no crinkle plays in the cut. If the edit keeps the camera plan's SH02B filter action instead, the alternate plays at f99-f105, picture-led: a dry paper crinkle as the folded filter goes in, then a soft push as fingertips press it to the cone wall, stopping dry at f105. The card 'Nobody gets you before the pour.' comes in with no sound: no sting, no whoosh.

cues.timing: D01-B3, 4.50-7.00 s: room tone 4.50-4.70 s (f108-f113); kettle tips 4.70 s (f113); stream lands 4.80 s (f115); bloom fizz rises from 5.30 s (f127); the stream breaks on the selected SH03 take's break frame, planned 6.58-6.83 s (f158-f164, target 6.71 s, f161); fizz alone from the break to 7.00 s; hard out on the cut at 7.00 s (f168). All picture-led, ±2
cues.description: Cause before effect. 4.70 s: off screen, water shifts inside the metal gooseneck kettle as it tips (only the spout is in frame). 4.80 s: the stream lands, a brief dry patter on the heaped grounds that becomes a thin stream on wet grounds by about 5.00 s (f120). It is heard close, just above the cone, and follows the spiral. From 5.30 s the bloom fizz rises underneath: a fine crackle of gas escaping as the grounds swell and dome. On the selected take's break frame, the kettle tips back and the last thread snaps off. From there to the cut, the fizz is the only focal sound. Backup if the fizz records too faint: from the break, the first brewed drops falling into the mug, from the same takes. Hard out at f168 with no tail, so 005's lift-off tick owns f168-f170. No music, as the script specifies.

cues.description: The same motor and the same pulse as B1. It starts with the edge glow at 9.2 s (f221) and stops dead at 10.0 s (f240), the frame the rattle stops and the rings flatten. In B1 her hand cut the pulse short at f19. Here nobody touches the phone, so it runs its full 19 frames and stops on its own. PROP-02 lies face-down on its four corner pads, 1.5 mm proud of the glass, and the glass never touches. The hum reads thinner through the pads, the four pads chatter on the oak, and the corner pad against the chipped mug ticks fast. NORA's fingertips rest lightly along the mug's side, palm clear, so each tick keeps only a brief, damped ceramic edge. Because it is coupled into the counter and the mug, it reads wider and flatter than B1, through contact and level, and it is the loudest moment of the spot. The coffee's rings make no sound, and no liquid sound is added. Then room tone alone, the quietest stretch, while her fingertips stay put (no foley). The card 'Everyone else gets you at 7:05.' comes in with no sound.

cues.timing: D01-B5 to D01-B6, 11.50-15.00 s: room tone 11.50-11.79 s (f276-f283); kettle ticks at 11.79 s (f283) and 12.25 s (f294) in B5, and at 13.58 s (f326) and 14.46 s (f347) in B6; last decay gone by 14.67 s (f352); room tone to 15.00 s (f360)
cues.description: The metal kettle cools off screen on the burner at 214/100. That puts it hard right and slightly behind camera, about 95° right of the 55° lens axis, roughly 1.4 m from C4/C5 at lens height. Pan the ticks hard right. Each tick is small, dry and metallic: the metal contracting after the B3 pour, which is the cause. The spacing is uneven and each tick is a little quieter than the last, so it never becomes a clock. The ticks aren't tied to picture, so the editor can slide any of them, but keeps each one at least 4 frames clear of every card-in. Re-checked against the current script's card-ins at 11.50 s (f276, 'Hand-glazed stoneware.') and 13.00 s (f312, the CTA): f283 is 7 frames after f276, f294 is 18 frames before f312, f326 is 14 frames after f312, and f347 is clear. They are also clear of the earlier review's f264 and f300: f283 is 19 frames after f264, and f294 is 6 frames before f300. The script has the ticking run to the last frame. It runs through B6, but the last tick has died by 14.67 s, so nothing is cut off at the last frame, and room tone runs to 15.00 s at the 0.00 s level so the loop is clean. No music, sting or logo sound under any card: the product stays a silent hero.

The current script beats are B1 f0-f36, B2 f36-f108, B3 f108-f168, B4a f168-f204, B4b f204-f276, B5 f276-f312 and B6 f312-f360. Every hit is picture-led, ±2 frames.

Phone physics follow PROP-02 as built, per the world bible as quoted in the notes: four corner pads 1.5 mm proud of the glass, bumper open along all four edges, flat case back with no raised camera module. Face-down it rides on the pads and the glass never touches: the pads knock and chatter on the oak, and a corner pad ticks against the mug. The session records on a case built to that spec. B4b hand: fingertips rest lightly on the mug's side with the palm clear, per the script. They damp the mug less than a full wrap would, so the pad ticks keep a brief, damped ceramic edge. The coffee rings are silent.

evidence.specificity: Every hit has a source, a material, a time and a frame, and the frame maths checks (for example 2.79×24=66.96→f67, 8.46×24=203.04→f203, 13.58×24=325.92→f326). The editor and foley stage can work straight from lines like "1.88-2.00 s (f45-f48): as the Solace dripper lifts off the dish rack, its stoneware foot knocks one coated-wire tine and slides clear. Light, dry, one contact." and "At 1.25 s (f30) the phone lands face-down on its four corner pads, which stand 1.5 mm proud of the glass: one soft, low knock of the pads on wood, with no bounce and no glass sound, because the glass never touches." It stops short of 9 for two reasons. First, the B4b conflict is flagged ("On the camera plan the rattle runs f221-f240 (0.79 s), so a card at f228 lands mid-buzz. The sound follows the camera plan."), but the plan gives no cue timing for the case where the script's timing wins. Second, the kettle that is poured in 004 and cools in 007 has no stated state in B1-B2.
evidence.distinctiveness: Much of this could only belong to this film. The atmosphere removes the clock for a reason tied to the idea: "a clock tick (the phone's 7:00 is the only clock)". The turn is heard through this script's own objects: "the four pads chatter on the oak, and the corner pad against the chipped mug ticks fast. NORA's fingertips rest lightly along the mug's side, palm clear, so each tick keeps only a brief, damped ceramic edge." The product is heard as itself: "recorded ... on a production sample of the Solace dripper, so the stoneware you hear is the product's own." Two things hold it at 8. The room-tone bed ("a fridge compressor's low, steady hum ... a thin wash of street traffic through a closed window") is stock city-flat tone, and the plan never says why this route wants it. The central sound rhyme also rests on two frames. "In B1 her hand cut the pulse short at f19. Here nobody touches the phone, so it runs its full 19 frames" is not true of the timings given: B1 runs f2-f19, which is 17 frames, so no listener will hear the hand cut it off.
evidence.fit: The plan serves R1's "Sound carries more of the emotion than music" and the script's no-music decision exactly. It says "No music anywhere in D01 ... The editor lays no temp track either: a temp bed would mask the B4b buzz, which is the turn," and puts the turn at the top of the arc: "Arc: the loudest moment is the B4b buzz, 9.21-10.00 s (f221-f240) ... The quietest is the tone alone straight after it (f240-f283), where the refusal lands." It stays off unsupported claims and says so: "'Dense stoneware' is a sound direction only. The verified facts appear only in the silent cards." The product role is heard in use (seat click, lift-off, set-down on oak), and the hero hold is kept silent. Two things hold it at 8. B4b departs from the script's picture line (rattle from the top of the beat, stopping "about 1.0s in") to follow camera-plan frames. It flags this, but the only version it gives is the one that moves the turn. It also ends the script's "kettle ticking ... to the last frame" at 14.67 s. That change is justified by the ring-out rule and stated openly.
evidence.craft: The core technique is right. Cause comes before effect ("4.70 s: off screen, water shifts inside the metal gooseneck kettle as it tips" before "4.80 s: the stream lands"). Every hit is marked "picture-led, ±2". Ring-outs die before the last frame and the loop is matched: "the last tick has died by 14.67 s, so nothing is cut off at the last frame, and room tone runs to 15.00 s at the 0.00 s level so the loop is clean." The case physics hold together. Rights are named by source, scope and owner and none is claimed as cleared: "Needs a written assignment of the recordings and all rights in them from the foley artist and the recordist, covering all media, worldwide, in perpetuity ... Status: session and assignment pending. Owner: producer." The library fallback scope is labelled an assumption. It needs small notes, not real ones. "Pan the ticks hard right" is a mix decision, and hard right is risky in a vertical feed. Stale history is still in the working plan ("They are also clear of the earlier review's f264 and f300", "The client's f238 is inside ±2"). The lift-off tick is placed on the exact cut frame ("the first sound of the new shot"), and a drip into coffee is given "the mug's short hollow ring".

notes.target: SND-D01-002 and SND-D01-006 (the B1/B4b pulse rhyme)
notes.note: The plan says her hand cuts the B1 pulse short. It plays f2-f19, which is 17 frames, against B4b's full 19 frames, a 2-frame difference nobody will hear. Pick one fix and write it into both cues. (a) Drop the 'cut short' claim and put the contrast where it is audible: B1 is face-up, flush and bright, and its oak chatter stops the moment the hand lifts the phone off the wood; B4b is on the pads, coupled into the mug, the loudest moment of the spot, and stops dead on its own. (b) Flag the film director that the hand has to land by about f12 for the B1 pulse to be audibly cut before its natural end at f21. Whichever you choose, record the pulse at 24 frames or longer so it also covers the script-timed B4b alternate.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Every effect serves an action on screen or a story event off it'; quality bar, Distinctiveness (the idea-specific detail has to survive into what is heard)

notes.target: SND-D01-006, SND-D01-001 arc, and the B4b FLAG in assumptions
notes.note: Add the script-conform alternate so the editor does not have to call. notes.target: SND-D01-001 atmosphere (the kettle's state before the pour, and why the traffic is there)
notes.note: 004 pours from a hot kettle and 007 has it cooling on the burner, but 001 never says what the kettle is doing off screen in B1-B2. Write one line with the choice and the reason. Either it is already on the heat off screen right, with a faint burner hiss under the room tone that stops across the B2/B3 time cut and is kept well under the B1 buzz, or it is absent because she puts it on during the B2/B3 cut. In the same pass, give the far traffic a reason tied to R1 (for example, the day already moving outside, kept behind glass) or cut it, so the bed is not stock city room tone.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'An atmosphere names what's heard, off screen too, and what's absent and why'; 'Cause before effect'

notes.target: SND-D01-007 kettle ticks (perspective)
notes.note: Replace 'Pan the ticks hard right' and the lens-angle arithmetic with a perspective direction: off screen right and behind camera, at room distance of about 1.4 m, smaller and drier than the on-screen stoneware, never closer than the dripper. Hard panning belongs to the mix. In a 9:16 feed heard on one earbud or a phone speaker, a lone hard-right tick either sits in one ear or pulls attention off the dripper during its only hero hold.
notes.source: Review brief: detail that does a later department's job costs craft; craft brief: 'Name the source, action, material and perspective'; taste notes: 'The product is a tool, then a hero'

That is about 21 cm, average 0.36 m/s, peak 0.58 or less. 20-25f: release; the fingertips open off the glaze, and R rises 2 cm. 25-36f: R travels about 15 cm back (peak 0.53 or less). The heel is on the oak by 33f and the pads are on the glaze by 36f. A late drop shifts everything after it, and SH05's tail absorbs the shift.
shots.performance: No hurry, no look. She waits out the drip over the mug. A claw grip over the rim, with the palm clear of the spent collar.

shots.purpose: D01-B4b · The phone rattles against the mug, rings bend TILE-01's reflected edge in the coffee, and her hand stays put · must-have (the turn). Generator risks: the rings and a dead-still hand. Method: practical only, with no composited rings. The face-down edge glow is composited to a reference plate. The ring read is proved in the pre-shoot test (blocker 2). If it fails, SH05 becomes its own 100mm take, cut at the settle (8.5 s).
shots.framing:

It holds the hand, the coffee and the phone; the dripper falls partly out frame-right. The coffee still mirrors TILE-01's edge from the same position, and the card sits on the oak below. Cut at 8.5 s, with 5 still frames after the join. This is a 1.5x cut-in, one size step: the CD's fallback, declared.
shots.lens_intent: 65mm at 1.39 m, f/11, as SH04. Sharp: the coffee surface, the knuckles, the phone edge and the dripper.
shots.lighting: SH04's light state, 3:1. From C4 the coffee centre mirrors wall D at about y 318, 119.6 cm. That is TILE-01's top edge (119.5): pale #D5D8D2 tile under #6B6E67 paint, and it is the edge the rings bend. It sits above the frame top. Prove it in the ring test on a 6-inch phone at 100%, in this frame. The phone glow is about 6500K, composited to a reference shot at this exposure, spilling 5-15 mm (ASSUMED).
shots.action: 0-5f: the hand is still. 5f (8.71 s): the phone lights face-down, buzzes, rattles 3 mm or less and ticks against the mug; fine rings bend the tile edge in the coffee. 24f (9.5 s): the rattle stops, the glow goes off, and the phone settles back against the mug. The rings are flat by about 30f (9.75 s), as the card comes up. 30-72f: the hand holds. Cut.
shots.performance: Nothing in the hand moves: no flinch, no squeeze, no drift toward the phone. The rings come from the phone, never from her grip.

shots.purpose: D01-B5+B6 · The empty dripper, whole, glaze pool to the lens, beside the dark phone's edge and the bare oak where the mug stood · must-have hero, 3.5 s. Generator risks: drift on a static hero, and a fabricated pool would be fake proof of hand-glazing. Method: a practical locked plate of the real unit, no retouch. The exterior has no mark, so nothing is tracked on.
shots.framing:
S4: a same-axis 1.7x cut-in on the 11.5 s time jump. C5 is at 149/221, 163 cm, on C4's line 14 cm nearer: +7, nearly her eye height, as if the lens takes her place. 37° down.
- The dripper sits 3-4 cm right of centre: rim at 38-86% w, 16-46% h, 47% of frame width.

- The case's face-down corner holds at the frame-left edge as a dark wedge (0-16% w, 16-26% h, about 4.6 cm of case in frame).
- SUPER ZONE for both cards and the sign-off: bare oak below the dripper at 50-64% h, 8-84% w, never over the dripper or the case. The wall-D card area is above the frame, which meets wall D at about 94 cm.
- Out of frame: the cable, WIN-01 and TILE-01.
- Product full.
shots.lens_intent: 100mm at 1.25 m (25 cm wide), f/16 (-7/+8 cm), focused on the front glaze arc. Sharp: the whole dripper, front rim to back rim. At f/11 (±5 cm) the front rim, 5.7 cm nearer, would soften. The case's nearest corner is about 16 cm behind the focus plane, so it falls soft and reads as a dark wedge. Nearest soft: the foreground oak. Pool read estimate: the 12 mm arc is about 42 px of 1080, against a 40 px mark (a hypothesis). Test variant: 100mm at 1.15 m (23 cm wide).
shots.camera_movement: Locked off. One hold; the cards change at 13.0 s (36f) in post.
shots.lighting: Key: the WIN-01 unit from frame-left, 4400K against a 5400K WB, raised 1 stop for f/16. Fill: the CEIL-01 bounce, 3:1. A black flag with a lens port sits at C5. The frame-left flank and the rim are the brightest detail. The pool mirrors, bottom to top: the clean oak in front of the foot, the wall-B flat, the lens flag (a small dark shape), CEIL-01, and at its up-facing top TILE-01's edge as a thin pale line (world bible). WIN-01's diffusion glints on the frame-left flank. No kicker, no retouch, no steam. The phone is dark.
shots.action: Nothing in frame moves from 0f to 84f.

shots.framing:
4:5, a separate practical plate, not a crop. The double stays on N2; no cheat.
C6 at 178/269, 167 cm: +11, behind and beside her right shoulder, 20 cm wall-A of her chest line. Bearing 55°, the dripper's front to the lens. 53.5° down.
It is on 55°, not the suggested ~70°, because at 70° her shoulder enters frame-left. The frame top sits on WIN-01's sill line, so the copy moves to the oak below.
Placements (±5%):
- Rim at 61-90% w, 17-28% h; body to 35% h; mug to 45% h. Whole and unobstructed.
- Kettle body at 7-40% w, 13-32% h, scorch band at 30-32% h.

- COPY ZONE: bare oak at 55-92% h, 8-92% w.
Monitor checks: no sash at the top edge (if it shows, tilt 1° down); no hip bottom-left; R out.
shots.lens_intent: 50mm at 0.82 m to the cone, f/11 (-8/+10 cm), 1/200 s sync. Sharp: the bloom, the stream, the rim, the scorch band and the phone. Nearest soft: the oak at the frame bottom.
shots.lighting: Key: a strobe fired through WIN-01's diffusion frame, imitating the window, gelled to 4400K against a 5400K WB, from frame-left. Flash duration t0.1 of 1/2000 s or shorter, which holds a 5 mm stream moving at about 0.8 m/s to 0.4 mm of travel. Fill: the passive aisle bounce, 4:1. The continuous light is kept 4 stops under the flash, so nothing ghosts. The stream is edge-lit, and the dark bloom sits in white paper. The phone is dark. No added steam.
shots.action: Frozen as the second outward circuit lands on the dome (about 5.7 s in SH03's timing).

shots.purpose: D02-2 · The empty dripper alone and whole, glaze pool to the lens · must-have still (the DTC image). Generator risk: the pool is the proof of hand-glazing. Method: practical, the real unit, no retouch.
shots.framing:
4:5, a separate plate on bare oak. The phone, cable and mug are struck, and the foot is on the ring mark.
C7 at 146/219, 124 cm: 32 cm under her eye line, at counter-eye level for the product view. Bearing 55° (the pool's own bearing), 15° down.
- The dripper is centred at 50% w, 50-82% h, 44% of frame width.
- The wall-D base is at about 55% h behind it.
- TILE-01's lower edge is at about 7% h, and the course runs out the top.
- COPY ZONE: the wall-D paint at 8-40% h, between the tile edge and the counter.
- WIN-01 is out.
shots.lens_intent: 100mm at 1.1 m, f/16 (-5.5/+6 cm), focused 2.5 cm behind the front glaze arc. The rim band reads as a shallow ellipse, with the pool square to the lens. Sharp: the front rim to the back rim. Nearest soft: the oak 10 cm in front. Wall D is soft.
shots.lighting: Key: the WIN-01 unit from frame-left, 2.5:1. The balance is neutral: key and WB are matched on the 18% card (5000K and 5000K), so the DTC image shows the #E3D9C6 body and the #B59A72 pool true. This is a deliberate difference from D01's warm balance. Fill: the CEIL-01 bounce, with a black flag and lens port at C7. At 15° down the pool mirrors the clean, evenly lit oak in front of the foot and the wall-B flat; the rim band mirrors CEIL-01 and the flag. The cream body is the brightest detail.

assumptions: D01 runs at 24 fps because the spec gives none (logged): 36+24+48+60+36+72+84 = 360 frames = 15.0 s. The beat boundaries fall at B1 36f, B2 108f, B3 168f, B4a 204f, B4b 276f and B5-B6 360f. The D02 stills are logged at 24 fps, 0 frames.

Lenses are full-frame equivalent: 9:16 on 20.25 x 36 mm, 4:5 on 24 x 30 mm. Frame percentages are pinhole estimates from the world-bible marks, ±3% (±5% for SH07); confirm them on the monitor. Depth of field uses a 0.03 mm circle of confusion.
No platform template was given, so I assume a safe band at 15-65% of height and an icon rail over the right 12% of width, from 40% to 90% of height.

Key: a unit behind WIN-01's diffusion frame, imitating an east window at 7:00 in early November. It runs at 4400K against a 5400K WB in D01 and D02-1. SH08 is balanced neutral on purpose. ASSUMED; meter on the day.
Hand speeds assume bell-shaped moves, with the peak about 1.6x the average, held to the treatment's 0.6 m/s. The final check is frame to frame on the take.
The '7:00' digit height is 2.4 cm, per ART-LOCK-0700. That is about 60-75 px in SH01's 34 cm frame, leaning about 42° on screen.
Coffee mirror: from C4 the coffee centre mirrors wall D at about y 318, 119.6 cm, which is TILE-01's top edge. This is a geometric estimate, confirmed in the ring test.
NORA is 167 cm (eye 156, shoulder 137). N2 and the rack mark come from the treatment.
Product size and glaze come from the world bible and are ASSUMED; no reference was inspected.

Deliberate departures: (1) SH02A runs 24f, not the treatment's 18f, per the client and CD notes. The seat click stays at absolute f67. (2) SH04's arc takes 14f, not 10f, because 21 cm in 10f would peak at about 0.8 m/s. (3) SH06 and SH08 are at f/16, so the whole dripper stays sharp with focus on the front arc, and the case still falls soft. (4) SH07 is on 55°, not ~70°. (5) The card zones are set on screen, not in the wall-D card area. (6) The fill for SH04-SH06 and SH08 is a CEIL-01 bounce with a lens flag, so no light shows in the gloss.

Closed per the director's rulings: rack out of SH01 (1), the phone's end kept in SH03 (3), the wrist over the port in SH05 (5), the B2 split and the one SH04-SH05 take (4). The PD's grommet puts OUT-01 below the top, out of every frame and reflection. The filter stack is gone from B2 (script).

Taste notes followed: hands before faces (no face anywhere); no slow motion (100% speed); no window and no gazing; the product as a tool before it is the hero; the end frame on the product, not a logo card. One break, the script's call: S2's scorch band is out of D01 so the bloom stays large; it reads in SH07.

blockers.issue: Hand-double release is pending. The double's hands appear in the SH01, SH02A, SH02B, SH03 (pouring), SH04 and SH05 plates and the SH07 still, and may be used as a generator reference.
blockers.resolution: Secure a release from the double's agent covering the D01 and D02 plates and reference use before any plate is shot or fed to generation.

blockers.issue: SH05's ring read is unproven. At 65mm and 1.39 m the coffee is about 1.2 × 0.7 cm on a 6-inch screen, and the turn depends on the rings visibly bending TILE-01's reflected edge.
blockers.resolution: Schedule the pre-shoot ring test on the built set, in SH05's frame, with the unit's top cut in place, judged on a 6-inch phone at 100% with the card on. If it passes, shoot SH04-SH05 as one take. If it fails, shoot SH05 as its own take on the 100mm fallback, cut at 8.5 s.

blockers.issue: The treatment places the cards in the wall-D card area (125 cm and up). In SH02B that area falls at 0-11% h, above the safe band, and it is above the frame in SH02A and SH04-SH06. The screen zone that stays clear in SH02B (16-26% h) lies over TILE-01's course.
blockers.resolution: Approve the screen zones: 16-26% h in B2, bare oak in B4b and B5-B6. The storyboard checks card legibility over the tile band in SH02B.

blockers.issue: Not yet verified: the pool read in SH06 and SH08 (estimated at 42 px), the gloss read and the mirror contents with no rig, the real rim diameter (casting needs 10.5 cm or more), and the f/16 sharpness of the real unit.
blockers.resolution: Supply the real unit for a camera test at the SH06 and SH08 frames, graded on a 6-inch phone at 100% with the cards on. Keep 1.25 m if it passes, move to 1.15 m if not, and refer to the director and copywriter if both fail.

blockers.issue: Route departure: R1 asks for a 'handheld-but-steady' camera, and every shot here is locked. The '7:00' composite, the product's own output at 100mm, the S3 take and the S4 hold all need stillness.
blockers.resolution: Approve the locked grammar with Lucas, or approve handheld for S1 only, at the cost of a tracked '7:00' composite.

evidence.specificity: Quote: "C4 at 139/215, 171 cm: +15, bearing 55°, 37° down, panned 3° toward wall C. This is the widest D01 frame." and "65mm at 1.1 m (34 cm wide), f/8. Sharp: the phone glass and the mug rim. Nearest soft: the counter's front edge." Every shot states its position, height, bearing, lens, distance, stop, what is sharp and soft, frame percentages, Kelvin, ratio and frames. The geometry holds against the world-bible marks. From C1 the phone at 230/304.8 is 1.09 m away, at bearing 54.9° and 49.5° down. SH05's coffee mirror point recomputes to 119.6 cm with the world-bible formula. A storyboard artist or generation supervisor could act on it without a follow-up call. It is not a 10 because a few lines rest on sources the package does not carry ("per ART-LOCK-0700").
evidence.distinctiveness: Quote: "From C4 the coffee centre mirrors wall D at about y 318, 119.6 cm. That is TILE-01's top edge (119.5) … and it is the edge the rings bend." SH06 is "focused on the front glaze arc". Swap in a machine-glazed cone and SH02A's thumb pass, SH06's focus point and its pool-mirror plan all break. The camera-height arc also belongs to this idea: it ends at C5, "+7, nearly her eye height, as if the lens takes her place". It stays at 8 for two reasons. The camera grammar itself (locked off, 55° from the aisle, window key three-quarter back) is standard tabletop work. And the hero's light currently favours the flank, not the pool.
evidence.fit: Quote from the SH05 fallback: "the dripper falls partly out frame-right." The script keeps the dripper "in frame for the whole beat", and route R1 says "It stays in frame through the pour, the bloom, and the final held mug". Blocker 2 says the ring read is unproven, so this fallback is likely to be used, and it weakens the product's role at the turn. The first touch of the verified fact is also outside the plan's own safe band: "The dripper stands at 38-62% w, 66-75% h". Otherwise the fit is close. It makes no claim beyond the verified facts. "Taste notes followed: hands before faces (no face anywhere); no slow motion (100% speed); no window and no gazing". It holds a 3.5 s readable product close, and it sends the route's handheld-to-locked departure to the director rather than deciding it.
evidence.craft: Quote from SH02A: "0-5f: R arrives from frame-left. Index and middle fingers hook the near rim, and as the grip closes the thumb lands at the foot and sweeps up across the pool to the rim band without stopping". That is an entry, a hook and a sweep of about 9 cm in 0.21 s. Under the treatment's 0.6 m/s cap it cannot be performed. Also: "This is a 1.5x cut-in, one size step: the CD's fallback, declared" is a cut on the same subject with less than 30° and fewer than two size steps. And "per the client and CD notes" overrides ruling 6 on notes that no page in the package carries. Against that, the arithmetic is professional throughout: "36+24+48+60+36+72+84 = 360 frames = 15.0 s", the SH03 f/16 depth of field (±4.8 cm), and "Flash duration t0.1 of 1/2000 s or shorter, which holds a 5 mm stream moving at about 0.8 m/s to 0.4 mm of travel".

notes.target: SH05 · framing (FALLBACK) and purpose
notes.note: The fallback reads "100mm lens from C4's position, re-aimed about 6° toward wall C … the dripper falls partly out frame-right … This is a 1.5x cut-in, one size step". It fails three ways. It drops the product the script keeps in frame for the whole beat. The cropped side of the dripper lands in the plan's own icon rail (right 12% of width, 40-90% of height). And a 6° re-aim with one size step on the same subject is a jump cut. Rebuild it where the treatment put it. At a bearing of about 40°, the world-bible mirror formula puts the coffee's mirror point at y≈327, on TILE-01, and the sightline to the mug crosses x 195 at y≈250, so her torso stays out. By the marks, a frame about 27-28 cm wide from there (100mm at about 1.36-1.38 m) holds the whole dripper left of the rail, the mug, the hand, and the phone's mug-side edge with its contact point. The port end can leave frame-left. Solve the height with the formula so the coffee centre mirrors the 119.5 cm edge; that comes out near 26° down, with the lens near 160 cm. Check that WIN-01's wall-C jamb stays out of the top-left corner, since it is only a degree or two outside at that aim. Then restate the coffee's size on screen, and declare the cut as a swing of about 15° plus a size change of about 1.6x.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'A cut to the same subject changes angle 30° or size two steps' and '…clear of the sides and the right-hand icon rail'. Script decision: 'In B4b the dripper stands in frame on the side away from the phone'. Route R1 product_role: 'It stays in frame through the pour, the bloom, and the final held mug'. Treatment S3: 'on a bearing between 31° and 55° … the dripper stays in frame for the whole beat'. World bible: the coffee mirror line formula.

notes.target: SH02A · action and framing (and SH02B's opening)
notes.note: The first 5 frames cannot be performed. At the 0.6 m/s cap, the hand needs about 6 frames just to cross from frame-left to a rim at 38% w. This sweep is also the only place the verified 'hand-glazed' is shown before B5 names it. Re-budget the shot at whatever length the director rules: 0-6f entry and hook; 6-14f the thumb sweep from foot to rim band (about 9 cm at about 0.27 m/s); then the lift, easing into the set-off in the last frames. Open SH02B earlier in the carry, with the dripper entering frame-right over about 12 cm as the treatment had it. That way the cut doesn't join 0.45 m/s on the way out to 0.24 m/s on the way in. Also move the resting dripper out of '66-75% h', which is below the plan's own 15-65% band, where the platform caption sits. Tilt about 4-5° down so it rests near 51-60% h and the top of the lift stays under about 37% h, clear of the 16-26% card zone. Flag TILE-01's bullnose down where the tilt puts it behind the card.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'In 9:16, faces, product and text sit about 15–65% of frame height'. Quality bar, craft: 'timing that can be performed, … nothing physically implausible'. Treatment S1: 'Peak hand speed is about 0.6 m/s or below'. Script decision: 'The fact is shown in use before it is named'.

notes.target: SH06 · lighting (and SH08 · lighting)
notes.note: The purpose is 'glaze pool to the lens', but the lighting says 'The frame-left flank and the rim are the brightest detail' and lets 'WIN-01's diffusion glint on the frame-left flank'. So the eye lands on the one part a competitor's cone shares. The front faces 235°, on the fill side of a wall-C key, so the pool reads only through what it mirrors. Choose one of the brief's two reads and light for it. Option one: make the pool's upper fillet the brightest specular in frame. Its normals at about 35-64° mirror CEIL-01 from wall B to overhead, so give the ceiling bounce a defined, even patch above and behind C5, and state its size and level. Option two: declare the pool 'darker and edge-lit', read by that band plus TILE-01's pale line. In either case, net the key on the frame-left flank so it stops being the brightest detail, and state the pool's value against the body. SH08's lighting also names 'The cream body' as the brightest detail. At 15° down the pool's upper fillet still mirrors CEIL-01, so make the same choice there.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'The focus subject is the brightest detail, or darker and edge-lit, as purpose says'. World bible product_placement: the swap test and the pool's mirror path. Taste notes: 'The product is a tool, then a hero'.

notes.target: assumptions (Deliberate departures) and SH01 lens_intent
notes.note: Three references don't match the package. (1) 'SH02A runs 24f, not the treatment's 18f, per the client and CD notes' overrides ruling 6 ('SH02A's 18 f stand') on notes that no upstream page carries. Cite them, or move the change into a director blocker next to blocker 5. (2) 'The seat click stays at absolute f67' is not right. The treatment's click, SH02B f15 after an 18-frame SH02A, falls at about f69, so say it moves about two frames earlier. (3) 'per ART-LOCK-0700' cites an ID that appears in no upstream page. Cite the world bible's lock-screen spec instead, and log the 2.4 cm digit height as ASSUMED. Also drop the SH03 pass mark ('judged on a 6-inch phone'): acceptance checks belong to the generation supervisor.
notes.source: Quality bar, craft: 'every cross-reference to another department's IDs is right'. Treatment S1 action_progression: 'SH02A's 18 f stand (ruling 6)'. Quality bar: 'Detail that does a later department's job … costs craft'. Craft brief: 'prompts, references and acceptance checks are the generation supervisor's'.

notes.target: SH01 · framing and lens_intent
notes.note: The hook's only text leans: "'7:00' leans about 42° frame-right". It has 0-19f before the hand lands, and the 7:05 payoff depends on that read. With the phone's top toward wall D, the lean on screen is atan(cos β / (sin β · sin δ)), where β is the camera bearing and δ the down angle. At C1's 55° bearing and 50° down that gives 42.5°, which is steeper than the treatment's '35° off upright'. Move C1 to about a 65° bearing and 60° down at the same 1.1 m (near 180/281, at about 187 cm), and the lean drops to about 28°. The sightline then crosses x 195 at about y 288 and 159 cm, roughly 10 cm clear of her head. Confirm that on the monitor, along with her upper arm at the flip, and check that the mug and its tide line still hold frame-right in the 34 cm frame. If her head blocks the swing, just go steeper: 55°/70° gives about 37°.
notes.source: Script decision: 'The readable 7:00 sets up the 7:05 card'. Treatment SH01 flag: "with the digits about 35° off upright, '7:00' reads on a 6-inch phone at 100%". Craft brief: 'Keep every shot describable as a visible result'.

notes.target: SH07 · framing
notes.note: Two locked items sit inside the shot's own '±5%' placement tolerance. The first is the scar joint at '0-4% w, 4-12% h'; the style bible makes that scar the pouring hand's continuity lock in D02-1. The second is 'The frame top sits on WIN-01's sill line', and the world bible keeps the window out of every frame. Lock both in a frame test at C6 on the built set before the shoot day. Aim to have the index finger's middle joint at least 6% inside the frame edge and the top edge at least 5% below the sill. If the two can't both hold, keep the sill out first and take the conflict to the director, rather than cropping the scar.
notes.source: Style bible continuity lock: '[any frame showing the back of the left hand, at least D02-1 on the kettle handle] One pale, flat, matte 10 mm scar'. World bible: 'The window is never in frame, and nobody looks out of it'. Taste notes: 'Anyone gazing out a window holding a mug'.

The frame budget '36+24+48+60+36+72+84 = 360 frames = 15.0 s', with 24 fps logged as an assumption and the stills as 0-frame entries.
The camera-height arc descending to C5 at '+7, nearly her eye height, as if the lens takes her place', with contrast easing from 5:1 to 3:1.
SH05's coffee-mirror light plan (TILE-01's 119.5 cm edge at y≈318, with a top cut on the unit) and 'Practical only, with no composited rings'.
SH06: 100mm at 1.25 m, f/16, focused on the front glaze arc; a practical locked plate with no retouch; supers on bare oak below the dripper, clear of the icon rail.
SH03: f/16 depth of field (±4.8 cm), 100% speed, and 'Nothing is added to the steam or the foam'.
SH07's strobe freeze ('t0.1 of 1/2000 s … 0.4 mm of travel'), with the continuous light 4 stops under.
One axis for the whole spot (every lens in the aisle on the wall-A side, wall C frame-left) and the exit-right/enter-left from SH01 to SH02A.
Sources declared as imitations ('imitating the 7:00 window (declared)', the CEIL-01 bounce 'as the room's return (declared)') and the black flags with lens ports for the gloss.

contradictions_flagged: CLAIM · SH02A-SH08 (every panel that shows PROP-01). The world bible still reads 'Shape and size are ASSUMED ... no dimensions, colour or finish were supplied', so the handle-less cone, the cream glaze, the speck, the rim band, the foot pool and the raw foot are all assumed. Only 'Hand-glazed stoneware', 'Dishwasher safe' and 'Made in small batches' are verified. Script B5, B6 and D02-2 and camera plan SH06 and SH08 use the pool as the visual of 'Hand-glazed stoneware'. PROP-07's Mark 1 ring (seen in SH04) is sized to the assumed Ø 10.0 foot, and the bible marks it ASSUMED because it needs a raw foot. What breaks: any product frame generated or dressed from these words shows a product nobody has confirmed. If the real unit has no pool or a different foot, the hero frames and the DTC image show features it lacks, and the ring shows outside the foot. Owner: producer (production sample and brand sign-off), then the production designer and copywriter. Fix: supply a brand-confirmed real-sample reference before any product frame is generated or shot, and run camera plan blocker 6 (the gloss read test) on it. If there is no pool, the copywriter revises the B5/B6/D02-2 picture; if the foot differs, the production designer recuts the ring. The panels mark these reads ASSUMED. Also a producer blocker.

ROUTE CAMERA · SH01-SH08. Route R1's visual_language asks for a 'handheld-but-steady camera'. The camera plan locks every shot ('Every shot is locked', its declared departure, blocker 8). What breaks: the route outranks the camera plan, and the departure isn't approved. The SH04-SH05 single take, both same-axis cut-ins (SH02B-SH03, SH05-SH06) and the '7:00' composite all depend on the lock, so unlocking means re-boarding them. Owner: cinematographer, for Lucas. Fix: Lucas approves the locked grammar, or the plan is redone handheld-but-steady and the board with it. Boarded locked. Also a producer blocker.

ROUTE LIGHT · SH08. Route R1's visual_language asks for 'warm low window light'. Camera plan SH08 lights neutral, with key and WB matched (e.g. 5000K on 5000K), 'a deliberate difference from D01's warm 4400K-against-5400K', so the DTC image shows the #E3D9C6 body and #B59A72 pool true. What breaks: the route outranks the camera plan, and the departure isn't approved. The D02 pair, which the script runs together, puts a warm still 1 (SH07) beside a neutral still 2. Owner: cinematographer, for Lucas. Fix: Lucas approves the neutral DTC still, or the cinematographer also shoots SH08 warm so Lucas can choose on the plates. Boarded neutral. Also a producer blocker.

S2 DETAIL · SH03. Script B3's picture says 'NORA's hand tips a gooseneck kettle', and the world bible names the kettle's gas-scorch band as S2's one real detail (taste note 'One real detail per scene'). Camera plan SH03 frames the kettle body, the scorch band and R out frame-left ('per the treatment, the bloom's size wins'), leaving only the spout. What breaks: D01's B3 shows neither its scene detail nor the hand the script puts in it, and the taste-note break isn't declared. Only D02-1 (SH07) shows the band. Owner: director (declare or fix), with the cinematographer and copywriter. Fix: either the director declares the SH03 break on purpose (SH07 carries the band) and the copywriter makes B3's picture spout-only, or the cinematographer holds the band and the fingertips at the frame-left edge. Boarded as framed. Also a producer blocker.

S4 DETAIL · SH06, SH08. The world bible names Mark 2, the forearm-worn front edge at x 197-201, y 250-330, as S4's one real detail ('she is gone and her wear stays'). Camera plan SH06 and SH08 don't place it: SH06 names only 'the foreground oak' as nearest soft, and SH08 'the oak 10 cm in front' of the foot. What breaks: S4, the 4 s hero and the DTC still, may carry no scene detail, which is an undeclared break of the taste note. Owner: production designer and cinematographer. Fix: the cinematographer confirms whether the front edge falls inside SH06 and SH08 and places it. If it doesn't, the production designer names an in-frame S4 detail in the bible, or the director declares the break (for example, keeping SH08 bare on purpose as the DTC image). Boarded without Mark 2. Also a producer blocker.

RACK · SH01. Script B1's picture ('a dish rack at frame right') and the bible's B1 frame lock (PROP-04) put the rack in the hook, but camera plan SH01 frames it out, 51 cm frame-right (its blocker 1). What breaks: the hand exits toward something the viewer hasn't seen, and the first look at the rack and the product falls to SH02A's 18f (see FIRST LOOK). The same blocker drives ELLIPSIS. Owner: cinematographer (blocker 1), with the copywriter and production designer if the rack leaves B1. Fix: hold the rack's edge at frame-right in SH01, or the copywriter drops the rack from B1's picture and the production designer drops it from the B1 lock. Boarded as the camera plan frames it.

B2 PICTURE · SH02A, SH02B. Script B2 describes one frame: the rack at frame right, the mug at frame left, and the dripper 'in the lower half of frame the whole way'. The camera plan splits B2 into two angles: the rack at centre-bottom (SH02A) and the mug at centre (SH02B), with the dripper's top at 43% h at the SH02A cut and 47% h once seated. What breaks: the card stays clear (the named zone keeps at least 9% clearance), but the script's picture no longer describes the frames, and 'lower half' is broken by 3-7%. Owner: copywriter. Fix: amend B2's picture to the two-angle version, replacing 'lower half' with 'below the card band'. Boarded as the camera plan frames it.

ELLIPSIS · SH01-SH02A. Camera plan SH01 ends with 'R carries on frame-right past the mug, toward wall A. Cut on the move', and SH02A opens with R arriving from frame-left and closing on the rim by 5f. But at SH01's exit the hand is still at least 51 cm short of the rack (camera plan blocker 1). From N2, her right shoulder (185/293) is about 93 cm from the dripper (232.7/213), so the treatment's 'she takes one step toward wall A' (as quoted in the film director's note) also falls in the cut. What breaks: read as a cut on action, the hand jumps at least 50 cm of reach plus a step in no frames, and SH01's exit doesn't equal SH02A's entry. Owner: cinematographer. Fix: hold more of the reach in SH01 (with the rack edge in frame, see RACK), or declare the cut a direction-matched ellipsis, as SH02A-SH02B already is. Boarded as planned and labelled a direction-matched ellipsis.

FIRST LOOK · SH02A. SH02A is the first look at the rack and at the product, and the B2 card lands on its f0, but the camera plan holds it for 18f (0.75 s), under the 1 s first-look minimum (the plan's pace fix, blocker 5). SH03 no longer names the feeling ("the tool at work" replaces "this is what the five minutes are"), which respects the script's decision never to name five minutes. evidence.craft: All five previous notes are addressed. (1) The cut is relabelled: "CUT after f35: a direction-matched ellipsis, not a cut on action". The ELLIPSIS flag names the cinematographer as owner, and check (6) now lists "SH01-SH02A (direction-matched ...)". (2) Board notes separate reads from texture: "TEXTURE (not a read): the pale ring at right (Mark 1, ASSUMED, see CLAIM)". (3) Flags are split by root cause (ROUTE CAMERA, ROUTE LIGHT, S2 DETAIL, S4 DETAIL), and blockers are split the same way. (4) tracked_elements follows one declared rule, "a panel is logged only where the element is in frame or heard", and PROP-06 SH03 is aligned: "held untipped 0-7f". (5) Every risk line now leads with its path: "PATH: practical only: a locked plate of the real unit, no retouch." The frame arithmetic checks out: 360f, the shot starts, and card rates of 10.7/15.5/14.7/14.8 cps. Two small gaps remain. First, the sleeve assumption contradicts the look lock "[every frame with her: D01-B1 to B4b, D02-1] The sleeve ends in the lower third of the forearm" and the camera plan's SH01 line "Her elbow reaches the frame-left edge at the flip". Second, SH03's "then the spout enters frame-left" contradicts the camera plan's "0-7f: the spout is held still over the dry heap" and the panel's own entry_state. Both are small notes, not rework.

The SH01-SH02A cut is labelled a direction-matched ellipsis, following the reviewer's note and the geometry (hand at least 51 cm short of the rack at SH01's exit; shoulder about 93 cm from the dripper). The camera plan's 'Cut on the move' is kept as timed, and the difference is flagged (ELLIPSIS).

Board notes separate READ (what must land at phone size in the frames given) from TEXTURE (seen but not claimed as learned), per 'Restraint over explanation'. The script's choice never to name 'five minutes' is kept out of the notes too.

tracked_elements follows the craft brief's rule: a panel is logged only where the element is in frame or heard. Off-frame positions stay in entry_state and exit_state. The one declared exception is NORA in SH03: the camera plan lists her, and her pour is the in-frame action, though her hand is out frame-left. PROP-06 is logged in SH06 as heard (SND-D01-007).

PROP-06 in SH03 f0-f7 is held at ST2's position, untipped (the camera plan's 0-7f hold). ST2 is boarded from the tip at 7f, and the kettle leaves frame tipped back, still in R, before its ST3 on the burner.

Every generation_risk line stays 'high', because each shot fails in a named way if generated. The PATH at the head of each line tells the generation supervisor whether a generator touches the shot at all, and SH06, SH07 and SH08 are marked real unit only because they prove a verified fact.
The ink-blue cuff is boarded in frame at the frame-left edge only in SH04-SH05, from the look lock for the widest counter frame (B4a). The camera plan doesn't place it.
The phone's screen goes dark as it lands face-down in SH01 (PROP-02 ST2), so the first edge glow is SH05's.
The cable is boarded as plugged in and off-frame in SH03 and SH06, following the bible's ST2 route; the camera plan doesn't place it in either shot.
The D02 stills carry no audio, and the sound plan covers D01 only, so SH07 and SH08 have no cues.
'7:00' and '7:05' frame the ritual. They are not a brew-time or performance claim (a hypothesis for the producer to confirm).
No reference was inspected, because no reference_reader is bound. Positions and states come only from the camera plan and the bibles given here.
