blockers.issue: PROP-01's whole appearance (shape, size, colour, glaze, foot pool, raw foot) is still ASSUMED in the world bible ('no dimensions, colour or finish were supplied'). SH02A-SH08 all show it, script B5/B6/D02-2 and camera plan SH06/SH08 use the pool as the visual of 'Hand-glazed stoneware', and the PROP-07 Mark 1 ring is sized to the assumed foot.
blockers.resolution: Get the production sample and the brand's confirmation of its appearance, and supply a real-sample reference before any product frame is generated or shot. If the real unit differs, the copywriter revises the B5/B6/D02-2 picture and the production designer recuts the ring to the real foot.

blockers.issue: Route camera: every shot is locked off (camera plan blocker 8), against route R1's 'handheld-but-steady camera'. The departure is not approved.
blockers.resolution: Lucas approves the locked grammar before the shoot, or the camera plan is redone handheld-but-steady and the board with it.

blockers.issue: Route light: SH08 (D02-2) is lit neutral (key and WB matched, e.g. 5000K on 5000K), against route R1's 'warm low window light', and it pairs with a warm SH07. The departure is not approved.
blockers.resolution: Lucas approves the neutral DTC still, or the cinematographer also shoots SH08 warm and Lucas chooses on the plates.

blockers.issue: Taste note 'One real detail per scene' is broken, undeclared, in SH03: the kettle's scorch band (S2's detail) and NORA's hand from script B3 are framed out frame-left.
blockers.resolution: The director declares the SH03 break on purpose and the copywriter makes B3's picture spout-only, or the cinematographer holds the scorch band and fingertips at the frame-left edge.

blockers.issue: Taste note 'One real detail per scene': S4's detail (Mark 2, the forearm-worn front edge) is not placed in SH06 or SH08.
blockers.responsible_agent: producer (production designer and cinematographer to place it, or director to declare)
blockers.resolution: The cinematographer confirms Mark 2 inside SH06 and SH08. If it isn't there, the production designer names an in-frame S4 detail in the bible, or the director declares the break.

blockers.issue: The hand double's release is still pending. She is a real person, and SH01, SH02A, SH02B, SH04, SH05 and SH07 rely on her hands.
blockers.resolution: Get a signed release covering paid social, the DTC site and the stills before any hand plate is shot or used as a generation reference.

evidence.specificity: Every panel gives the generation supervisor frames, cue IDs, positions and hand states. For example SH02B: "SND-D01-003 from f16: seat click f16 (picture click 13f); filter crinkle and press f30-f38 (picture drop and press 45-51f); see SYNC". Its exit reads "R empty, fingers 2 cm above the filter collar, still ... PROP-05 (ST2): one filter in the cone; stack of 7 at 252/308". NORA's body position is now written into every state: "stepped off N2 toward wall A, at the rack" and "hips back at N2". It stops short of 10 because a supervisor building SH01, SH02A or SH02B would still have to ask what the sleeve is doing. The assumption "The ink-blue cuff is boarded in frame at the frame-left edge only in SH04-SH05" leaves the sleeve out of three panels where the camera plan puts the forearm in frame.
evidence.distinctiveness: The reads only work for this idea. SH05: "With the sound off, the rings plus the card tell it: the day reached her cup and got nothing. '7:05' answers SH01's '7:00'." SH06: "The dark phone wedge at frame-left and the bare oak where the mug stood say she took the coffee and left the phone." The continuity locks are just as particular to this project, such as "Mirror check: the mole is on the back of the right hand only." Swap in another pour-over and the phone-against-mug geometry, the rings and the 7:00/7:05 pairing all break.
evidence.fit: Claims come first and are held to the verified facts: "CLAIM · SH02A-SH08 (every panel that shows PROP-01). The world bible still reads 'Shape and size are ASSUMED ...'". The panels that carry fact copy are marked real-unit only: "This shot PROVES A VERIFIED FACT ('Hand-glazed stoneware.' card), so it needs the real product." The route departures are now separate decisions Lucas can take one at a time ("ROUTE CAMERA · SH01-SH08", "ROUTE LIGHT · SH08"), each with its own producer blocker. Check (11) confirms the taste notes are held: "no face, no window, no music, no slow motion, and the product is in the last frame." SH03 no longer names the feeling ("the tool at work" replaces "this is what the five minutes are"), which respects the script's decision never to name five minutes. Both must-includes are boarded: the product as the thing the refusing hand goes to, and a 96f readable hero.
evidence.craft: All five previous notes are addressed. (1) The cut is relabelled: "CUT after f35: a direction-matched ellipsis, not a cut on action". The ELLIPSIS flag names the cinematographer as owner, and check (6) now lists "SH01-SH02A (direction-matched ...)". (2) Board notes separate reads from texture: "TEXTURE (not a read): the pale ring at right (Mark 1, ASSUMED, see CLAIM)". (3) Flags are split by root cause (ROUTE CAMERA, ROUTE LIGHT, S2 DETAIL, S4 DETAIL), and blockers are split the same way. (4) tracked_elements follows one declared rule, "a panel is logged only where the element is in frame or heard", and PROP-06 SH03 is aligned: "held untipped 0-7f". (5) Every risk line now leads with its path: "PATH: practical only: a locked plate of the real unit, no retouch." The frame arithmetic checks out: 360f, the shot starts, and card rates of 10.7/15.5/14.7/14.8 cps. Two small gaps remain. First, the sleeve assumption contradicts the look lock "[every frame with her: D01-B1 to B4b, D02-1] The sleeve ends in the lower third of the forearm" and the camera plan's SH01 line "Her elbow reaches the frame-left edge at the flip". Second, SH03's "then the spout enters frame-left" contradicts the camera plan's "0-7f: the spout is held still over the dry heap" and the panel's own entry_state. Both are small notes, not rework.

notes.target: NORA entry_state/exit_state and tracked_elements in SH01, SH02A, SH02B; generation_risk in SH01, SH02A, SH02B, SH05; the assumption 'The ink-blue cuff is boarded in frame ... only in SH04-SH05'
notes.note: Correct the assumption. The look puts the sleeve in every frame with her, and the camera plan puts the forearm in frame in SH01 ('Her elbow reaches the frame-left edge at the flip') and SH02A ('only the forearm enters'). In each panel where her forearm is in frame, write the sleeve state into NORA's entry and exit: #1F2A40 felted sleeve ending 7 cm above the wrist bone at rest and 9 cm reaching, a 4 cm felted cuff, bare wrist and hand. Add the same state to her tracked_elements row. Add the cuff failure mode to those panels' generation_risk lines (a crisp or ribbed cuff, sleeve under 5 cm, a second fabric), as SH04 already does. Where the camera plan doesn't say how much forearm shows (SH02B), flag the cinematographer instead of assuming either way.
notes.source: Look NORA_L01 lock: '[every frame with her: D01-B1 to B4b, D02-1] The sleeve ends in the lower third of the forearm, 7 cm above the wrist bone at rest and 9 cm reaching, never under 5 cm'; Craft brief: 'entry_state and exit_state write out ... each character'; 'When sources conflict, board what you were given and flag the owner'

notes.target: SH03 board_note ('The eye drops into the dry heap, then the spout enters frame-left') and SH02B cut line ('the spout is arriving')
notes.note: Both lines have the spout arrive after the cut. The camera plan says '0-7f: the spout is held still over the dry heap', and SH03's own entry_state already places it there. Rewrite both so the spout is in frame and waiting at f0. The read becomes: the eye drops into the dry heap under the waiting spout, and the stream starts at 7f. A generator or editor working from the note would otherwise animate an entry the plan doesn't have.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Never re-time, re-frame or re-order a shot'; 'board_note is what the frame reads as'; Quality bar craft: 'continuity that holds'

notes.target: tracked_elements NORA SH03; SH05 exit_state 'PROP-02 (after ST3)'
notes.note: Apply your own logging rule without an exception. In SH03 NORA is neither in frame nor heard; the kettle tip in SND-D01-004 belongs to PROP-06. Either drop her SH03 row and keep her position in entry/exit_state, or log her as heard through that cue the way PROP-06 is logged heard in SH06. Replace 'after ST3' with the bible's state name and position (face-down, dark, at 230.0/302.8, touching the mug), so every state label points to an existing bible state.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'tracked_elements holds ... one "entry → exit" state per panel it appears in, citing only existing shot IDs'; the board's own assumption on the logging rule

keep: CLAIM as the first flag, with the pool, foot and Mark 1 ring marked ASSUMED in every panel that reads them

The READ / TEXTURE split in every board note, and the cut lines that give type and reason ('direction-matched ellipsis', 'same-axis cut-in ... (escalation)', 'straight cut to the wide ... (geography reset)')
NORA's standing position (N2 / at the rack / back at N2) written into every state and into her track, plus the ELLIPSIS flag with the cinematographer as owner
The PATH lead on every generation_risk line, with SH06, SH07 and SH08 marked real-unit only because they carry verified-fact copy
The SYNC flag: in-shot and absolute frames, six named misses, and exact target frames for the sound designer
Separate ROUTE CAMERA, ROUTE LIGHT, S2 DETAIL and S4 DETAIL flags, each with its own producer blocker
Word-for-word copy with card rates, the cue windows (room tone alone ranges), and the 360f / shot-start arithmetic in the checks
The mole mirror check in every panel with NORA's hand, and the hand-double release blocker with its scope

jobs.method: Practical reference capture at the wardrobe fitting with the contracted hand double, not generated. Outputs CHR-NORA-HAND@v1 and LOOK-NORA-L01@v1. Attached to SH01 as its first use. It is the check reference for SH01, SH02A (and its fallback), SH02B, SH04, SH05 and SH07.
jobs.prompt: Reference set of the hand double's hands and forearms in the felted ink-blue house pullover, laid on an oiled oak offcut beside a centimetre ruler, soft even light from camera-left, pores and knuckle creases sharp. Views: back of the right hand, back of the left hand, both palms, the thumb side of the right middle finger, both forearms flat at rest, then reaching forward, with the cuff edge and wrist bone in every forearm view. Skin matte, nails short and bare, fingers and wrists bare.
acceptance_checks: Mole and callus read on the right hand only. If they read on the left, the file is mirrored: reject.
The cuff edge sits 7 cm above the wrist bone at rest and 9 cm reaching, never under 5 cm, on both arms. Nothing on the fingers or wrists, and the skin is matte.
Skin value, hand shape (8.5 cm across the knuckles, middle finger about 7 cm) and nails are logged against the ruler, so the SH02A fallback's generated hand can be checked against them.
The double's signed release covers this capture before it is shot (see the release blocker).
jobs.capability_notes: No generator. The plates use this same double, so this set is the reference for the mirror and continuity checks. In the SH02A fallback it is a check reference only, because the profile's one slot carries the product.
jobs.estimated_cost_unit: 0 generation units; fitting time is the producer's

jobs.method: Practical reference capture of the brand-confirmed real sample (client photos or a studio packshot), not generated. Outputs REF-PROP01-SAMPLE@v1, views V1-V8. Each view can be cited alone (for example REF-PROP01-SAMPLE@v1:V3) to fill a one-slot generation. Attached to SH02A, its first use, since SH01 frames the rack out. It feeds SH02A to SH08.
jobs.prompt: Reference set of the real production dripper on a neutral grey card beside a centimetre ruler, soft even light from camera-left, sharp from rim to foot, surfaces untouched. The front (the thickest glaze arc at the foot, or the side the brand names if there is none) faces the lens unless stated. V1: fifteen degrees down (SH08). V2: thirty-seven degrees down (SH02B, SH04 to SH06). V3: forty degrees down, front turned thirty degrees off the lens (SH02A). V4: fifty-three degrees down (SH07). V5: straight down into the empty cone (SH03). V6: underside and foot. V7: seated on the chipped white mug. V8: lifted in the hand double's right-hand rim grip.
acceptance_checks: The ruler reads in every view, and the rim, height and foot diameters are logged in cm. A rim of 10.5 cm or more keeps glaze visible on both sides of the double's 8.5 cm knuckles; below that, casting re-checks the hand. If the foot is not 10.0 cm, the production designer recuts the ring.
Each view is labelled V1-V8 with its angle and front bearing. V3 shows the unit alone, so it can fill the fallback's single slot.
Brand sign-off lists which assumed features the real unit has (handle-less cone, cream satin glaze, speck, gloss rim band, uneven foot pool, raw foot band). No SH02A-SH08 plate is shot before it.
The exterior is unmarked, as made. Any maker's mark is on the underside only.
jobs.capability_notes: No generator. Product views come only from the real sample, CAD or a shoot. This file does not exist yet (CLAIM), and every product frame waits on it. V8 uses the hand double, so it needs the release.
jobs.estimated_cost_unit: 0 generation units; sample and packshot cost is the producer's

jobs.method: Pre-shoot practical glow test on the built set, at SH05's lock and exposure, with the re-specced phone case. Not generated. Outputs REF-PROP02-GLOW@v1, the state reference that PASS-SH05-GLOW@v1 and SH05-COMP must match. It can run in the same prelight as the camera plan's ring test.
jobs.prompt: Stills from SH05's locked position at its exposure, the room lit as for the take: the face-down phone in its charcoal case, riding on four corner pads at its mark, touching the white mug of coffee on the oiled oak. Its screen is lit underneath to a full bright field. Where light escapes the open edges, a thin cool spill lies on the oak, and the gap shows only soft, even light. One matching frame with the screen off. The frame holds only the counter set, and everything is still.
acceptance_checks: For each edge, the test logs whether light leaks, how far it reaches on the oak in mm, and its level in stops over the lit oak, all at SH05's exposure.
Nothing on the screen is legible through any gap, and no light falls on the mug.
It is shot on the case built to the bible (four corner pads 1.5 mm proud, open along all four edges). A case without the gap fails.
jobs.capability_notes: No generator, and no product reference needed. If no edge leaks, SH05-COMP adds no glow and the rings carry the beat, since the storyboard rates the glow a secondary cue.
jobs.estimated_cost_unit: 0 generation units; prelight time is the producer's

jobs.method: Practical plate, locked on a high arm, with the hand double. The rigged phone shows a blank lit field, buzzes until the hand lands, and cuts to dark on the landing frame. Outputs PLT-SH01@v1, which feeds SH01-COMP.
jobs.prompt: Steep view down onto the oak counter, window light from frame-left three-quarter back, soft fill from frame-right. A charcoal phone lies face-up just left of centre, its screen an evenly lit blank light-grey field, buzzing in place until 0.8 seconds, its cable running out frame-left. The white mug stands just right of it, and an opened paper filter lies on a stack at top right. At 0.8 seconds a right hand enters from bottom-left without slowing, thumb on the phone's frame-left long edge and fingertips on its mug-side edge. It lifts the phone two centimetres and rolls it face-down toward the mug. It lets go a centimetre above the oak with thumb and fingertips clear of the mug side, and the phone drops against the mug at 1.2 seconds. The screen is dark from that frame. The hand carries on out frame-right past the mug by 1.5 seconds. Phone glass and mug rim sharp; counter front edge soft. The frame holds the right hand and forearm below the cuff only, with the upper arm beyond the frame-left edge. Ambient kitchen room tone only.
acceptance_checks: The field is blank and evenly lit from 0 to 1.2 s, with no clock, date, notification or status text from the handset. It is dark from the landing frame at 1.2 s, and after that there is no light on the oak around the case.
The phone buzzes from 0 to 0.8 s and stops as the hand lands, with nothing vibrating in the hand. The hand lands without hovering and rolls the phone in one move, and the cable stays in the port.
At the release, a centimetre above the oak, no finger or thumb is between the phone and the mug. The phone falls the last centimetre on its own, and its edge knocks the mug.
No upper arm crosses the frame-left edge at the flip. Mole and callus on the right hand only.
Continuity: the phone ends face-down and dark, touching the mug. The mug and the stack with its opened filter are unmoved. The hand exits frame-right, and SH02A picks it up entering frame-left.
jobs.capability_notes: Practical, as boarded. Triage 7: screens 2, light switching 2 (the screen cuts at landing), reflections 1 (phone glass, mug glaze), fast motion 1 (habit-speed roll), cloth 1 (cuff). The phone is a prop, so there is no product contact. The alternatives are already in use (practical plus composite). If the rigged cut misses the landing frame, SH01-COMP paints out the leftover glow. The grip and release height are flagged to the director (blocker).
jobs.estimated_cost_unit: 0 generation units; shoot cost is the producer's

jobs.method: Composite: ART-LOCK-0700@v1 tracked onto PLT-SH01@v1's blank field; nothing is generated. Art spec: '7:00' only. Cap height is 2.4 cm on the 15 cm glass: about 53 px flat in SH01's 49 cm-wide frame, and about 45 px on screen after the 50-degree foreshortening. That figure is an estimate, and the measured height is the pass mark. Colour: #1B1F24 on #E4E7EA, centred in the upper half of the screen, upright to the phone, top toward the phone's top edge. Use a generic grotesque that is not any handset maker's lock-screen typeface or layout. The landing fingers are rotoscoped over the art, and any leftover glow after 1.2 s is painted out. Outputs COMP-SH01@v1.
jobs.prompt: The phone's lit field carries only the supplied time, 7:00, in dark plain digits centred in the upper half of the screen and upright to the phone, so they lean about 42 degrees frame-right with the handset. The art stays pinned to the glass while the phone buzzes and reads at phone size for the first 0.8 seconds. As the hand rolls the phone, the fingers pass in front of the art and it turns away with the glass. From the landing at 1.2 seconds the screen is dark and the oak around the case matches the unlit plate. The frame holds the right hand and forearm below the cuff only. Ambient kitchen room tone only.
acceptance_checks: Measured along the digits' height, 7:00 is at least 45 px tall in the 1080-wide frame. It reads on a 6-inch phone at 100% within the first 0.8 s, leaning with the phone, with no date, status bar, icon or extra glyph.
No OS trade dress is imitated: no shipping handset's lock-screen typeface, clock layout, wallpaper, lock icon, status bar or notification style.
The art tracks the glass through the buzz and the roll with no slip. The landing fingers stay in front of it with clean roto edges. There is no light on the oak after 1.2 s.
jobs.capability_notes: Post composite of designed art. The digits are never generated, because generated digits garble or pick up a date or status bar. Triage as SH01-PLT.
jobs.estimated_cost_unit: 0 generation units; design and compositing time are the producer's

jobs.method: Practical plate with the real unit and the hand double, locked off. Outputs PLT-SH02A@v1.
jobs.prompt: Looking down over the near wires of a white wire dish rack that fills the bottom of frame, window light from frame-left behind, the white plate held a stop darker than the dripper. The dripper stands upright in the rack in the lower third, the brightest shape, beside the plate, an upturned tumbler and a fork. A right forearm and hand enter from frame-left moving right and close on the dripper by 0.2 seconds in a one-hand rim grip: fingertips over the rim, thumb on the outer wall, glaze showing on both sides of the hand. By 0.6 seconds it lifts about twelve centimetres, foot clear of the wires, with no turn in the hand. Then it sets off level toward frame-left and away, still moving at the cut at 0.75 seconds. Rim and hand sharp; front wires soft. The frame holds the right hand and forearm below the cuff only. Ambient kitchen room tone only.
acceptance_checks: The rim grip holds from 0.2 s to the cut, with glaze showing on both sides of the hand. Silhouette and surface match REF-PROP01-SAMPLE@v1 (V3), with no added handle or mark and no turn in the hand.
No wire passes through a finger or the foot. At the cut the dripper is moving frame-left and away, with its top at 43% of frame height or lower.
The card zone (16-26% height, 10-86% width) holds no hand, dripper or rack part for the whole take, and the plate reads darker than the dripper.
Continuity: the empty right hand enters frame-left moving right (SH01 exits frame-right). Plate, tumbler and fork are unmoved. Mole and callus on the right hand only.
jobs.capability_notes: Practical. Triage 5: hand-on-product 2, fast motion 1 (0.5 m/s lift), cloth 1 (cuff), reflections 1 (gloss rim band). Conditional fallback: SH02A-FB-IMG, then SH02A-FB-VID. Trigger: by the end of SH02A's slot (8 takes, assumed), no take passes both the wire-clear and the front-turn checks, and the director chooses the fallback over a pickup. The fallback covers a failure on the day, not a missing input: it needs the same sample and release as this plate, plus Lucas's ceiling.
jobs.estimated_cost_unit: 0 generation units; shoot cost is the producer's

jobs.method: Conditional text-to-image hero still with the product reference in the single slot. It runs only on the trigger in SH02A-PLT. It opens on the closed rim grip because image-to-video would invent the entering hand. Outputs STL-SH02A-FB@v1 for SH02A-FB-VID. This changes the approved shot, because the hand's entry from frame-left is lost. That is flagged to the director, not made.
jobs.prompt: A metre off, forty degrees down over the near wires of a white dish rack along the bottom. The dripper stands upright in it, front slightly toward the lens, beside a plate, tumbler and fork. A right hand grips its rim: fingertips hooked over, thumb on the outer wall, glaze showing either side. Broad square hand, short blunt fingers, medium-deep warm brown skin, creased knuckles, short bare nails, a small flat dark-brown mole on its back two centimetres wristward of the middle knuckle. The forearm leaves frame-left into a flat ink-blue felted sleeve. Window light from frame-left behind, the plate dimmer than the dripper. Rim and hand sharp, front wires soft; the top quarter plain soft wall.
acceptance_checks: Hand, checked against CHR-NORA-HAND@v1: the skin value is no lighter, greyer or olive. The hand is broad and square with short, blunt fingers (middle finger shorter than the palm is wide). Nails are short, bare and straight-filed, with nothing on the fingers or wrist. There is one flat mole on the back of the right hand, 2 cm wristward of the middle knuckle, and none on the left. A missing or moved mole fails.

Product, checked against REF-PROP01-SAMPLE@v1:V3: silhouette, glaze and foot match, with no handle, mark or deformed cone. The front is about 30 degrees off the lens, glaze shows on both sides of the grip, and no wire passes through a finger or the foot.

Continuity with SH02A's entry: the dripper stands upright in the rack at 38-62% width and 66-75% height, beside the dry plate, tumbler and fork. The plate is darker than the dripper. The 16-26% height band holds no hand, dripper or rack part. Where the cuff shows, it is one flat ink-blue with no ribbing.
jobs.capability_notes: The frame needs product, hand and rack identity, but the profile takes one reference. REF-PROP01-SAMPLE@v1:V3 goes in the slot. The hand is written from text and checked against CHR-NORA-HAND@v1 at visual lock. Output is 1024 px. Try first, at 0 units: the best take's frame at 0.2 s (grip closed, dripper still in the rack). If it passes these checks, it becomes STL-SH02A-FB@v1 and this job is skipped. Triage 4: hand-on-product 2, reflections 1, cloth 1. The alternatives are the practical plate itself and that take frame.
jobs.estimated_cost_unit: Conditional. 1 still x 2 variations x (1 + 2 rounds) = 6 images at 1024 px worst case. Price unknown; it runs only under Lucas's approved ceiling. 0 if the take frame passes.

jobs.method: Conditional image-to-video from the approved still STL-SH02A-FB@v1. It runs only after that still passes visual lock. Outputs CLIP-SH02A-FB@v1; the edit takes 18 frames starting at the end of the half-second hold.
jobs.prompt: The frame holds still for half a second. Then the hand lifts the dripper straight up twelve centimetres in under half a second, foot clearing the wires, grip and front unchanged. It sets off level toward frame-left and away, still moving at the clip's end. The rack stays still. The camera stays locked off. Ambient kitchen room tone only.
acceptance_checks: After the half-second hold, the lift reads within the first second: straight up about 12 cm, with the foot clearing the wires and no wire through a finger or the foot.

Grip, front and silhouette hold through the lift and the carry: no turn in the hand, no handle growing, no cone deforming. The SH02A-FB-IMG hand checks against CHR-NORA-HAND@v1 hold in every frame, with the mole on the right hand only.

Continuity with SH02A's exit and SH02B's entry: at the cut point, 0.75 s after the hold ends, the dripper is moving level toward frame-left and away, with its top at 43% of frame height or lower. Plate, tumbler and fork are unmoved, and the top band is clear.
jobs.capability_notes: The inputs fit the profile: one image, a 5 s clip, 24 fps, 9:16, locked off, no seed or negative prompt. The output does not: the profile delivers 720p, and this clip is cut between 1080x1920 practical plates, with no verified upscale path. Fallback: Lucas accepts 720p for 0.75 s, or an upscale path is sourced and checked before the job runs. Triage 5: hand-on-product 2, fast motion 1, cloth 1, reflections 1. A generated lift can still push a wire through a finger, the practical's own failure; the checks catch it.

jobs.prompt: Looking down over the woman's right shoulder onto the white mug at centre, window light from frame-left three-quarter back, soft fill from frame-right. It drops the dripper two and a half centimetres onto the rim with a click and lets go by 0.6 seconds, its front square to the lens. The hand passes three centimetres above the far end of the face-down phone at left and pinches the opened top filter off the stack behind by 1.4 seconds. It drops the filter into the cone at 2.0 seconds and presses once with two fingertips, leaving a one-centimetre collar, then lifts two centimetres and stops by 2.25 seconds. Rim, collar and phone edge sharp. The frame holds the right hand and forearm below the cuff only. Ambient kitchen room tone only.

One filter only (the stack goes from 8 to 7) and one two-finger press. The collar sits about 1 cm over the rim, and the fingers are still 2 cm above it at the end.
The hand never touches or nudges the phone, which stays face-down and dark against the mug throughout.
The card zone (16-26% height, 10-86% width) holds no hand, dripper or stack, and the hand's highest point stays at 35% height or lower. The cable and outlet in that band must be gone (OUT-01 fix).
Continuity: the dripper enters moving right to left, as SH02A leaves frame-left and away. Mole and callus on the right hand only.
jobs.capability_notes: Practical insert. Triage 5: hand-on-product 2 (carry, seat, press into the cone), fast motion 1 (0.52-0.62 m/s), cloth 1 (cuff), reflections 1 (gloss rim band, mug). Compound action flagged: seat, release, cross over the phone, pick one filter, drop, press and lift, all in 2.25 s. It stays one take and is not split.

jobs.method: Practical plate at 100% speed with the real unit, real water and real grounds, locked off. No ramp and no added foam or steam. Outputs PLT-SH03@v1.

Then one thin stream circles twice, centre out and back, stopping short of the paper, and the grounds darken, swell and dome. From 2.1 seconds the stream stops clean, and the spout leaves frame-left by 2.4 seconds. The bloom fizzes alone to 3.0 seconds, all at real speed. jobs.prompt: The widest counter frame, from the aisle side, window light raking from frame-left, soft fill from behind the camera, the dripper the brightest shape. In one arc it moves frame-right until the foot clears the mug, then down onto the ring mark on the oak, on the mug's far side from the phone. Reference IDs (REF-PROP01-SAMPLE@v1, CHR-NORA-HAND@v1, LOOK-NORA-L01@v1, REF-PROP02-GLOW@v1, PASS-SH05-GLOW@v1, PLT-SH01@v1 to PLT-SH06@v1, STL-SH07@v1, STL-SH08@v1, ART-LOCK-0700@v1, STL-SH02A-FB@v1, CLIP-SH02A-FB@v1) are placeholders for files still to be shot, made or supplied. Review notes that the storyboard supersedes: (1) The front bearing is 235°, square to every bearing-55° lens, with no turn in the hand, so prompts say 'square to the lens', not '125°'. SH02A's lens is 30° off it. (2) SH06 is a 1.7x cut-in with no registration, so the cut-in checks replace the registration check. (3) The earlier SH01 grip note (thumb on the aisle edge, fingers on the wall-B edge, roll toward frame-left) doesn't fit the storyboard, where the phone ends against the mug at frame-right. SH01-PLT uses thumb on the frame-left edge and fingertips on the mug side, releasing 1 cm up (blocker to the director).

Resolved upstream and written into the jobs: right hand only; a single buzz, with the rattle from 0 to 0.8 s in SH01 and 0.2 to 1.0 s in SH05; the thumb stays still; card zones named; marks agreed; the SH07 ring wiped and cable struck; the mug in SH01.

Kit indexing follows the craft brief (a kit job attaches to the first shot that uses it): KIT-NORA-HAND at SH01, KIT-PROP01-SAMPLE at SH02A (SH01 frames the rack out), KIT-PROP02-GLOW at SH05. Each kit's method lists the shots it feeds.

Timings are in-shot seconds at 24 fps, from the camera plan's action frames: SH01 f19 = 0.8 s, f29 = 1.2 s, f36 = 1.5 s; SH02A f5 = 0.2 s, f14 = 0.6 s, f18 = 0.75 s; SH02B f11 = 0.5 s, f15 = 0.6 s, f33 = 1.4 s, f47 = 2.0 s, f54 = 2.25 s; SH03 f7 = 0.3 s, f50 = 2.1 s, f58 = 2.4 s, f72 = 3.0 s; SH04 f8 = 0.3 s, f23 = 1.0 s, f36 = 1.5 s; SH05 f5 = 0.2 s, f24 = 1.0 s, f36 = 1.5 s, f38 = 1.6 s, f48 = 2.0 s; SH06 f96 = 4.0 s. The sound plan's differing cue frames (SYNC) are the sound designer's to move.

The '7:00' size is an estimate. The 49 cm frame gives 1080 ÷ 49 = 22 px per cm. The digit height runs along the phone's long axis, 35° off the lens bearing in plan and seen 50° down, which keeps about 85% of it. So 2.4 cm gives about 53 px flat and about 45 px on screen. The measured height on the comp is the pass mark.
The key light is from frame-left in every setup. Every lens sits on the aisle side with wall C at frame-left, and there is no reverse.

The style bible asks every prompt to restate the mole and the skin hex codes. The craft brief keeps identity in references and bans hex codes in prompts, so the mole and callus sit in acceptance checks against CHR-NORA-HAND@v1. One exception is declared: in SH02A-FB-IMG the one slot carries the product, so that prompt writes the hand in words, without hex codes, and its checks hold it to CHR-NORA-HAND@v1.

Prompts write each exclusion as the wanted state (the hand and forearm below the cuff only; the air over the rim is clear; bare oak on every side of the foot; only the spout enters). Acceptance checks still name what fails.
Triage scores only the craft brief's ten factors. The phone, mug and kettle are props, so handling them is not product contact.

Picture carries no speech. Every video prompt ends on ambient room tone only, and the sound designer owns all audio.

evidence.specificity: Lucas gets a decision he can make without a follow-up call. The last blocker asks him to "set a dollar ceiling for the two fallback jobs, and say whether 720p is acceptable for SH02A's 0.75 s or an upscale must be sourced first". It also lists what has to be true before anything runs: "the trigger has fired, REF-PROP01-SAMPLE@v1 exists and the release is signed". The worst case shows its working: "(18 + 12 + 12) ÷ 24 = 1.75 s, so one 5 s clip. 1 x 2 x (1 + 2) = 6 clips at 720p worst case. Price unknown". The trigger is concrete: "by the end of SH02A's slot (8 takes, assumed), no take passes both the wire-clear and the front-turn checks". Prompts time their actions in in-shot seconds that trace back to the board's frames ("SH02B f11 = 0.5 s ... f54 = 2.25 s"). One loose end: the only paid video prompt stops at "still moving at the clip's end", which gives no end point in a 5 s clip (note 2).
evidence.distinctiveness: No prompt could be moved into another project. SH05-PLT: "At 0.2 seconds the face-down phone touching the mug buzzes once and rattles a few millimetres against it, and fine rings cross the coffee under the hand." SH02B-PLT check: "One filter only (the stack goes from 8 to 7) and one two-finger press." SH01-PLT: "It lets go a centimetre above the oak with thumb and fingertips clear of the mug side, and the phone drops against the mug at 1.2 seconds. The screen is dark from that frame." SND-D01-009 assumes 'the picture is generated... native audio is muted', but every shot is now practical, so handling of production sound is unspecified. Fix: re-derive the B1 and B4b contrast from the real case, record on PROP-02, and state how practical-plate audio is used.

The script's B4b has 'One phone buzz', the route has 'a phone buzzing once', and the camera plan has 'one rattle'. The sound plan's default for SND-D01-002 and 006 is a double pulse, with single pulse only as an alternate. The storyboard substituted the single pulses as the main track, which the sound designer owns. Fix: make the matched single pulses the default in the sound plan, timed to the picture rattle.

The world bible's frame locks disagree with the camera plan's prop lists. The B1 lock includes PROP-03. The B2 lock includes PROP-02, but SH02 and SH03 keep the phone out. The B4a, B4b, B5-B6 and D02-1 locks include PROP-08, but the camera plan has 'Out: ... cable' and SH07 has 'cable out'. The B4b lock omits PROP-05, though the spent filter (ST5) stays in the dripper. PROP-03 ST4 says the hand leaves 'the handle and chip clear', while casting, the director and the camera plan put the thumb on the chip at 165° (practical plates only). Fix: restate frame contents shot by shot, including the SH07 cable state, and amend PROP-03 ST4.

PROP-07 ST1 leaves the ring and centre drip spot bare in D02-1. The SH07 marks put the phone at 48/268 and the mug at 27.3/295, either side of the ring at 27.3/280, so the ring likely falls mid-frame (storyboard SH07 RING). In a paid still, a pale ring with a coffee spot next to the product can read as a stain the dripper makes. The world bible keeps product-made marks out of D02-2 only. Fix: cheat the ring out for the still, or confirm it is out of frame.

The B2 card 'Nobody gets you before the pour.' runs across the SH02 to SH03 cut, but the camera plan names no super zone for either shot. In SH02 the dripper is at 50/50 and moving right. In SH03 the cone is at 38/50 and the stack at 62-88% width. Nothing keeps the card clear of the product, and it may jump at the cut (storyboard CARD ZONE; generation blocker holds SH02-PLT and SH03-PLT). Fix: name one zone, held across both shots, clear of the dripper's path and the hand.

The hook depends on '7:00' reading in 0.8 s, and it sets up the 7:05 payoff for muted viewers. The camera plan puts the phone at 43-58% of frame width (about 15%) at 35mm, 0.85 m, and gives no legibility pass mark. Only SH01-COMP's acceptance check tests it. QC estimate (pinhole, unverified): the digits render roughly 2-3 mm tall on a 6-inch screen. Fix: add a camera-test pass mark for digit height on a 6-inch phone, and tighten framing if it fails.

The storyboard says 'No source names NORA's working hand.' The director's S1 treatment states 'Hands: R does every action. L stays empty and off-frame for the whole spot', and casting says 'Right-handed'. The false flag became generation-plan blocker 3 ('Which hand does the work (HAND) is unconfirmed') and an open question to the director. Fix: retire the flag, keep the right-hand mirror checks, and cite the director's line. The cross-body reach is already staged with a step toward wall A.

The SH05-COMP acceptance check requires 'Glow on all four edges, 5-15 mm onto the oak'. The director requires the composite to match the practical reference 'in which edges leak, how far... how bright' and warns that 'a glow brighter or wider than the reference is physically implausible'. In the camera plan's framing, the phone's port end is off-frame-left, so four edges can't be checked in frame. The check as written pushes compositors to paint glow the prop doesn't make. Fix: change the check to match the reference pass, on the edges visible in frame.

Proof point 1 states as fact that 'each piece carries visible handmade variation, giving the object a tactile, one-of-a-kind quality that a mass-produced plastic or metal drip gadget cannot claim'. That is an inference and a comparison beyond the verified fact 'Hand-glazed stoneware', and the glaze-pool demonstration rests on it. Proof point 4 is labelled a 'category fact' but has no source. Fix: move both to hypotheses, or say 'assumption, confirm on the real unit'.

Severity rubric: critical means no product or hand plate can be shot or used legally until it is resolved. Major means it must be resolved before the shoot or picture lock. Minor means it must be fixed before post lock.

lenses.verdict: I'd put the idea in front of the client today: the script, the cards and the boards. 'Nobody gets you before the pour' and 'Everyone else gets you at 7:05' sharpen the route. The coffee rings are a real detail only this story has, and the spot follows the taste notes throughout: hands only, no window, no music, and a product-in-frame ending. I would not approve it for production today, because the grade stops at craft 7. Six sound hits are off picture, and the B4b buzz is out of step with its own picture. The B4b grip is written four different ways. The generation plan sizes '7:00' against the wrong frame width. The treatment and the world bible still carry blockers the camera plan has already resolved. The rings, which carry the turn with the sound off, reflect a flat wall that will hide them and fill about 1 cm of a phone screen. The product itself is still invented pending a real sample, and two route departures need Lucas's approval. Each fix is small and assigned to one department, and none of them touches the idea.

evidence.specificity: Every department can act without asking a question. World bible PROP-03: "Chip on the rim at bearing 195°: 7 × 4 mm, 2 mm deep, raw buff #CDBBA0 matte against the gloss, from a knock on the faucet." Script D01-B4b: "The phone rattles against the wood, and the coffee in the mug shivers into fine rings under her hand. The rattle stops, the rings flatten, and her hand stays where it is." One thing holds it below 10: some pages do a later department's job. The treatment sets lens bearings and frame widths ("about 65 cm across at the phone", B6 "about 22-23 cm"), and the camera plan then overrides them, so the two documents now describe different frames.
evidence.distinctiveness: Logline: "When the day buzzes again, it gets as far as the rings in her coffee and no further until 7:05." The coffee rings, the 7:00-to-7:05 pair and the dripper left beside the refused phone fail the swap test, because they only work for this route. What keeps it at 8: the opening gesture of turning a phone face-down is common in digital-wellbeing ads. Apart from the glaze pool, which is still assumed ("PROP-01 is invented"), any ceramic cone could play the dripper.
evidence.fit: "Nobody gets you before the pour." / "Everyone else gets you at 7:05." is Lucas's "five minutes that are only yours — marked by the pour", said more sharply. The script decision confirms "Only the three verified facts are stated." Both must-includes are built in: the dripper works as a tool from B2 to B4a and is the hero in B5-B6. Three things hold it at 8. Two route departures are unapproved: the camera is locked off although R1 asks for "handheld-but-steady", and SH08 is lit neutral although R1 asks for "warm low window light". And the readable closing moment rests on a product nobody has seen ("no dimensions, colour or finish were supplied").
evidence.craft: The storyboard's own check: "What breaks: six hits sit outside ±2f, and the buzz at the turn is out of step with its own picture." The B4b grip is described four ways. Script: "wrapped around the chipped mug". Casting: "touch the mug but don't grip it". World bible: "wraps the body over 225-315°". Sound: "hand around the mug". The generation plan sizes '7:00' in "SH01's 49 cm-wide frame", but the camera plan's 65mm at 1.1 m on a 20.25 mm gate gives about 34 cm. SND-D01-007 puts the kettle "behind camera left", but the burner at 214/100 is about 136 cm frame-right of C4 and C5. The treatment and the world bible still carry blockers the camera plan has already resolved. Rights and consents are handled correctly: all named, all left pending.

lenses.verdict:
Not approved for production today. The idea is a near-A: the dripper is the tool that draws the boundary, the rings in the coffee under a still hand are a detail only this story has, and the end frame keeps the refused phone in view during the CTA. The specificity is the best I've seen. But I can't shoot from these pages without a follow-up call:
- No real product unit has been seen, so every product frame is built on an assumption.
- The script says 'wrapped' where casting, the treatment and generation say 'resting', and the storyboard copied the script.
- Six sound hits sit off picture.
- The world bible's frame locks, outlet position and translight still disagree with the camera plan.
- The '7:00' art spec uses the wrong frame width.
- The pour is staged as a backhand for a right-hander.
- SH07's 1/1000 s at f/11 can't be lit on a small crew's continuous kit.
- About ten blockers addressed to me as director are still open.
The notes above make those decisions and send each change to its owner. With that conform pass and the sample in hand, this is a 9.

evidence.specificity: Every department works from the same measured marks. For example: "ST2-ST4 face-down at 230.0/302.8 (case x 222.3-237.7, y 299.0-306.6), 33-41 cm from wall C, its wall-A edge touching the mug at 232.7/299." The camera plan puts each prop at a stated percentage of frame, and the storyboard converts every sound hit to in-shot frames. Nothing is left to interpretation. The one thing keeping this from a 10 is that departments measure some of the same things differently: the SH01 frame is 34 cm in the camera plan and 49 cm in the generation plan, and the '7:00' digits are 1.8 cm in one and 2.4 cm in the other.
evidence.distinctiveness: The turn belongs to this spot and no other: "The face-down phone rattles against the wood... the coffee in it shivers into fine rings. The rattle stops, the rings flatten, and her hand stays where it is. Card: 'Everyone else gets you at 7:05.'" The ending is also specific. The mug is gone and the phone is still face-down where she left it, so the idea is still on screen during the CTA. It stops short of 9 because the opening, a phone turned face-down, is a familiar digital-detox image. The rings, the 7:00/7:05 pairing and the phone left behind do most of the work of making it Solace's.
evidence.fit: It meets the brief closely. "The product works as a tool from B2 to B4a and is the hero in B5-B6." It states only the verified facts: "Only the three verified facts are stated... Nothing is said about taste, speed or quality." The dripper is the mechanism of the choice, as R1's product_role asks. Two departures from the route are still unapproved. The camera plan says "Every shot in the plan is locked" where the route asks for a "handheld-but-steady camera". SH08 is lit neutral ("a deliberate difference from D01's warm 4400K-against-5400K") where the route asks for "warm low window light".
evidence.craft:
Each department's work is strong on its own terms, but the departments still contradict each other, so I can't shoot from these pages without a call.
- The script says "NORA's hand is wrapped around the chipped mug". Casting says "fingers resting along the mug's side below the rim, palm clear", and the treatment and the generation prompts follow casting. The storyboard still says "R wrapped around the mug".
- Sound cue 006 still reads "SH05 f36-f53", so the buzz runs f216-f233. The camera plan starts it later: "5f (9.2 s): the phone lights face-down, buzzes once." The storyboard lists six hits outside ±2 frames.
- The generation plan sizes the '7:00' art on "SH01's 49 cm-wide frame". The camera plan's 65mm lens at 1.1 m gives a 34 cm frame.
- The B3 pour puts R "at about 215/317 in front of her chest" with the spout "toward about 140°". For a right-hander facing 90°, that is a cross-body, backhand grip.
- SH07 asks for "f/11, 1/1000 s" from a diffused continuous window unit. A small crew can't light that.
- About ten blockers across the camera plan, storyboard and treatment are addressed to me as director and are still open.

lenses.verdict: This is clearly ours and it sells the right thing. The phone flip, the dripper as the tool that draws the boundary, the rings in the coffee and 'Everyone else gets you at 7:05.' make the product the mechanism of the ritual. It stays scrupulously inside the three verified facts. I would not approve it for production today. Every product frame is built on an invented dripper, since no sample or spec has been supplied. The departments contradict each other on the B4b grip, six sound-sync points, the phone case, the SH06 cut-in and the outlet in the DTC image. The CTA works only for organic ('link in bio'). The brand name first appears at 12.5 s. Two route departures (locked camera, neutral DTC still) are unapproved. Fix the notes above, get the real sample and my answers to the direction questions, and this is a 9.

evidence.specificity: Every department names a mark, a frame or a hex, down to the turn itself: "The face-down phone rattles against the wood, and the coffee in the mug shivers into fine rings under her hand. The rattle stops, the rings flatten, and her hand stays where it is." The props are just as exact: "A mug's ring has no centre spot, so the pair can only be a dripper's." It stops short of 10 because some of that detail has already drifted between departments (see craft).
evidence.distinctiveness: The card pair is ours and passes the swap test. "Nobody gets you before the pour." is answered by "Everyone else gets you at 7:05.", and the turn is a detail no other pour-over brand has: "The day reaches into her cup and gets nothing." It is held below 9 because the connecting shots are category-standard: hands on an oak counter, warm window light, a bloom close-up ("Hold on the bloom"). And a morning without the phone is a familiar digital-detox frame; only the 7:05 line and the rings lift it.
evidence.fit: The claims discipline is exactly what I pay for: "Only the three verified facts are stated... Nothing is said about taste, speed or quality, and the price stays off screen." The product is the mechanism, not a prop: "The product works as a tool from B2 to B4a and is the hero in B5-B6." Fit to the objective and the route has gaps. The CTA works for organic only ("'Link in bio' assumes organic placement"). The brand name first appears at 12.5 s. Two route departures are still unapproved: "Every shot is locked" against R1's handheld-but-steady camera, and SH08 is lit neutral against R1's warm window light.
evidence.craft: Each department's work is high-craft, but the departments disagree with each other. The storyboard's own audit: "six hits sit outside ±2f, and the buzz at the turn is out of step with its own picture." The script still says "NORA's hand is wrapped around the chipped mug" while casting sets "touching but not gripping". The sound plan's "1.2 mm silicone lip" contradicts the bible's "four corner pads stand about 1.5 mm proud". The treatment's "tightens a little, about 1.2x" contradicts the camera plan's "The 1.7x size change rides the ellipsis". And "OUT-01 ... sits at the top-left edge" of the DTC image. These are real gaps, not polish.
